<!-- lemma-9: body_md -->
\label{l.limit-max}
    Suppose that $F$ is compact, $E_j$ are closed in $F$, and $w_j$ are continuous on $F$ with $w_j \to w$ uniformly on $F$.  Call $E^* = {\limsup}^* E_j$. Then
    \[\max_{E^* \cap F} w = \limsup_{j \to \infty}\max_{E_j \cap F} w_j .\]
<!-- end lemma-9 -->
<!-- proof-12: body_md -->
Let $x^* = \mathop{\textup{argmax}}_{E^* \cap F} w$. There are $E_{j_k} \ni x_{j_k} \to x^*$ so
    \[\max_{E^* \cap F} w = w(x^*) = \lim_{k \to \infty} w_{j_k}(x_{j_k}) \leq \limsup_{j \to \infty} \max_{E_j \cap F} w_j.\]
    On the other hand let $y_j = \mathop{\textup{argmax}}_{E_j \cap F} w_j$. Take a subsequence $y_{j_k} \to y \in E^* \cap F$ and $w(y_{j_k}) \to \limsup_{j \to \infty} \max_{E_j \cap F} w_j$. Then
    \[\max_{E^* \cap F} w \geq w(y) = \lim_{k \to \infty} w(y_{j_k}) =  \limsup_{j \to \infty} \max_{E_j \cap F} w_j.\]
<!-- end proof-12 -->
<!-- lemma-10: body_md -->
\label{l.prec-ordering-convergence}
    Suppose that $F$ is compact, $E$ is closed in $F$, and {$u$ and $v$ are continuous functions with} $u \prec_E v$ on $F$. If $u_j \to u$ and $v_j \to v$ uniformly on $F$ and ${\limsup}^*E_j \subset E$, then $u_j \prec_{E_j} v_j$ for $j$ sufficiently large.
<!-- end lemma-10 -->
<!-- proof-13: body_md -->
Note that $u \prec_E v$ on $F$ is equivalent to $\max_{E \cap F} (u - v) < 0$. By Lemma \ref{l.limit-max} 
  \[0>\max_{E \cap F} (u - v) = \limsup_{j \to \infty} \max_{E_j \cap F} (u_j - v)\]
  So $\max_{E_j \cap F} (u_j - v) < 0$ for $j$ sufficiently large i.e. $u_j \prec_{E_j} v$ on $F$.
<!-- end proof-13 -->
<!-- proposition-5: body_md -->
\label{p.semilinear-limit-viscosity}
     Suppose that $\mathfrak{u}_{\varepsilon_j}$ solve \eqref{e.bernoulli-parabolic-semilinear} in $U \times (0,T]$ and $\mathfrak{u}_{\varepsilon_j} \to \mathfrak{u}$ locally uniformly in $U \times (0,T]$. Define $E:={\limsup}^*\{\mathfrak{u}_{\varepsilon_j}>\varepsilon_j\}$. Then $(\mathfrak{u},E)$ is a relaxed viscosity solution of \eqref{e.bernoulli-parabolic} in $U \times (0,T]$.
<!-- end proposition-5 -->
<!-- proof-14: body_md -->
We check the relaxed subsolution property and the supersolution property of the limit.

\emph{Step 1: Relaxed Subsolution Property.} Let $V \times (a,b]$ be a parabolic cylinder and ${\varphi}$ a smooth strict supersolution of \eqref{e.bernoulli-parabolic} on ${\overline{V} \times [a,b]}$ with $\mathfrak u\prec_{E} \varphi$ on $\partial_P(V \times (a,b])$. Suppose towards a contradiction that $\mathfrak u \prec_{E} \varphi$ does not hold true on $V \times (a,b]$. 
    
    {We first claim} that for $0 < \delta \leq \delta_0$ sufficiently small, ${(\varphi-\delta)}$ is still a smooth strict supersolution of \eqref{e.bernoulli-parabolic} on ${\overline V \times [a,b]}$ with $\mathfrak u\prec_{E} \varphi-\delta$ on $\partial_P(V \times (a,b])$:  Since $E \cap \partial_P(V \times (a,b])$ is compact $\varphi-\mathfrak u$ is a positive continuous function on that set $(\varphi-\delta)-\mathfrak u$ is also positive on $E \cap \partial_P(V \times (a,b])$ for sufficiently small $\delta>0$.  A similar argument using the continuity of $(\partial_t - \Delta) \varphi$ and $|\nabla \varphi|$ shows the interior strict supersolution property of ${(\varphi - \delta)}$. 

    Now since $\mathfrak u \prec_{E} \varphi$ fails on $V \times (a,b]$, there exists $(x_0,t_0) \in E \cap (V \times (a,b])$ with 
    \begin{equation}\label{eqn:contraMe}
    \mathfrak u(x_0,t_0) \geq \varphi(x_0,t_0).
    \end{equation}  We split into two cases; either (i) $\varphi(x_0,t_0) >0$ or (ii) $\varphi(x_0,t_0) \leq 0$. In case (i) choose $\delta>0$ smaller if necessary so that $\varphi(x_0,t_0) - 2 \delta >0$.   

    

    Define $E_j := \{\mathfrak u_{\varepsilon_j} > \varepsilon_j\}$.  Now consider $\varphi_{\varepsilon} := \Psi_{\varepsilon,\theta}(\varphi-\delta)$, where $\Psi_{\varepsilon,\theta}$ is defined in \eqref{e.profile-ep-def}. By Lemma \ref{l.well-prepared} there is $\theta>1$ depending on the strict supersolution property of $\varphi-\delta$ so that $\varphi_\varepsilon$ is a smooth strict supersolution {of the semilinear equation} (\ref{e.bernoulli-parabolic-semilinear}) with $|\varphi_\varepsilon -(\varphi-\delta)_+| \leq \varepsilon$. By the uniform convergence of $\varphi_{\varepsilon_j}$ to $(\varphi-\delta)_+$, $\mathfrak u_{\varepsilon_j}$ to $\mathfrak u$, and $E = {\limsup}^*E_j$ {--- which implies $${\limsup}^*(E_j\cap \partial_P(V \times (a,b])) \subset E\cap \partial_P(V \times (a,b])$$---} we {apply Lemma \ref{l.prec-ordering-convergence} to} find that 
    \begin{equation}\nonumber  
    {\mathfrak u_{\varepsilon_j} \prec_{E_j} \varphi_{\varepsilon_j}}\quad \text{ on } \partial_P(V \times (a,b])
    \end{equation} for $\varepsilon_j$ sufficiently small. {In particular this gives $\mathfrak u_{\varepsilon_j} \leq  \varphi_{\varepsilon_j}$ on $\partial_P(V \times (a,b])$,} and  by the classical comparison principle for (\ref{e.bernoulli-parabolic-semilinear}) we conclude that 
   \begin{equation}\label{eqn:contraDo}
    {\mathfrak u_{\varepsilon_j}\leq \varphi_{\varepsilon_j}} \quad \text{ in } V \times (a,b].
    \end{equation}  {With this, we aim to contradict \eqref{eqn:contraMe} in cases (i) and (ii).}
    
      First consider case (i) where $\varphi(x_0,t_0)-\delta>0$. Then 
      \begin{equation}\label{eqn:contradicted}
      0\leq \mathfrak u_{\varepsilon_j}(x_0,t_0) -\varphi_{\varepsilon_j}(x_0,t_0) \to \mathfrak u(x_0,t_0)-(\varphi(x_0,t_0) - \delta)>0,
      \end{equation} where the first inequality follows from \eqref{eqn:contraDo} and the second from \eqref{eqn:contraMe}, and we conclude derive a contradiction for $\varepsilon_j>0$ sufficiently small.  
      
      Next in the case (ii), where $\varphi(x_0,t_0) \leq 0$, $\varphi - \delta$ is smaller than $-\delta/2$ in a neighborhood ${\mathcal{N}\subset V\times (a,b]}$ of $(x_0,t_0)$. Then, by Lemma \ref{l.profile-super}\ref{part.profile-super-e} {and \eqref{e.profile-ep-def},} $$\varphi_{\varepsilon_j} \leq (1-c(\delta))\varepsilon_j\quad \text{ in }\mathcal{N}$$ for $\varepsilon_j>0$ sufficiently small. On the other hand $(x_0,t_0) \in E$ so there is a sequence $\varepsilon_{j_k} \to 0$ and $(x_k,t_k) \in E_{j_k}$ with $(x_k,t_k) \to (x_0,t_0)$. Thus, for $k$ sufficiently large $(x_k,t_k) \in \mathcal{N} \cap E_{j_k}$ and 
      \[\mathfrak u_{\varepsilon_{j_k}}(x_k,t_k) > \varepsilon_{j_k} >(1-c(\delta))\varepsilon_{j_k} \geq {\varphi_{\varepsilon_{j_k}}(x_k,t_k)},\] and we again derive a contradiction with \eqref{eqn:contraDo}.


\emph{Step 2: Supersolution Property.} We now check the supersolution condition, which is similar to the above argument.
Suppose $V \times (a,b] \subset\subset U \times (0,T]$ and $\varphi \in C^\infty(\overline{V} \times [a,b])$ is a smooth strict subsolution of (\ref{e.bernoulli-parabolic}) in $\overline{V} \times [a,b]$ with $\varphi \prec \mathfrak u$ on $\partial_P(V \times (a,b])$. We want to show $\varphi \prec \mathfrak u$ in $V \times (a,b]$. Suppose this fails, then there is a first touching point (from below) denoted by $(x_0,t_0)$ with $\varphi(x_0,t_0) = \mathfrak u(x_0,t_0)$.

As in Step 1, $\varphi+ \delta$ is also a smooth strict subsolution for all small $\delta$. Noting that $\varphi+ \delta \prec \mathfrak u$ is equivalent to $\varphi+ \delta \prec_{\overline{\{\varphi+\delta>  0\}}} \mathfrak u$ and that 
\begin{equation}\label{eqn:containerMe}
{\limsup_{\delta\to 0}}^* \overline{\{\varphi+\delta>  0\}} = \overline{\{\varphi>  0\}}
\end{equation}
 by the subsolution condition 
$$|\nabla \varphi| > Q \quad \text{ on }\partial \{\phi>0\}\cap\left(\overline{V} \times [a,b]\right),$$
 we apply by Lemma \ref{l.prec-ordering-convergence} to conclude for $\delta>0$ sufficiently small that 
 $$\varphi +\delta \prec \mathfrak u  \quad \text{ on }\partial_P(V \times (a,b]).$$
 
 
 We then consider $\varphi_{\varepsilon} := (\Phi_{\varepsilon,\theta}(\varphi+\delta))_+$, which is a {viscosity} subsolution of (\ref{e.bernoulli-parabolic-semilinear}) by Lemma \ref{l.well-prepared}. By uniform convergence of $\varphi_{\varepsilon_j}$ to $\varphi$ and $\mathfrak u_{\varepsilon_j}$ to $\mathfrak u$ along with Lemma \ref{l.well-prepared}\ref{part.gep-5} and \eqref{eqn:containerMe}, we again apply Lemma \ref{l.prec-ordering-convergence} to find that $\varphi_{\varepsilon_j} \prec \mathfrak u_{\varepsilon_j}$ on $\partial_P(V \times (a,b])$ for $\varepsilon_j$ sufficiently small. Application of the standard comparison principle for \eqref{e.bernoulli-parabolic-semilinear} then yields $\varphi_{\varepsilon_j} \leq \mathfrak u_{\varepsilon_j}$ on $V \times (a,b]$, but for small $\varepsilon_j$ this contradicts the fact that $\varphi(x_0,t_0)+\delta>\mathfrak u(x_0,t_0)$ (cf. \eqref{eqn:contradicted}).
<!-- end proof-14 -->
<!-- head-12: body_md -->
Let $V \times (a,b]$ be a parabolic cylinder and ${\varphi}$ a smooth strict supersolution of \eqref{e.bernoulli-parabolic} on ${\overline{V} \times [a,b]}$ with $\mathfrak u\prec_{E} \varphi$ on $\partial_P(V \times (a,b])$. Suppose towards a contradiction that $\mathfrak u \prec_{E} \varphi$ does not hold true on $V \times (a,b]$.
<!-- end head-12 -->
<!-- head-13: body_md -->
We now check the supersolution condition, which is similar to the above argument.
Suppose $V \times (a,b] \subset\subset U \times (0,T]$ and $\varphi \in C^\infty(\overline{V} \times [a,b])$ is a smooth strict subsolution of (\ref{e.bernoulli-parabolic}) in $\overline{V} \times [a,b]$ with $\varphi \prec \mathfrak u$ on $\partial_P(V \times (a,b])$. We want to show $\varphi \prec \mathfrak u$ in $V \times (a,b]$. Suppose this fails, then there is a first touching point (from below) denoted by $(x_0,t_0)$ with $\varphi(x_0,t_0) = \mathfrak u(x_0,t_0)$.
<!-- end head-13 -->
<!-- corollary-3: body_md -->
\label{cor:increasing}
    {Suppose that $\mathfrak{u}_{\varepsilon_j}$ solve \eqref{e.bernoulli-parabolic-semilinear} as in Proposition \ref{p.semilinear-wellposed} with $g$ a strict subsolution and $(\mathfrak{u},E)$ is as in Proposition \ref{p.semilinear-limit-viscosity}.}
    Then $\mathfrak{u}$ is monotonically increasing in $t$, $E = \overline{\{u>0\}}$, and $\mathfrak u$ is a viscosity solution of \eqref{e.bernoulli-parabolic} in $U \times (0,T]$.
<!-- end corollary-3 -->
<!-- proof-15: body_md -->
Let $\varepsilon_j \downarrow 0$ and $(\mathfrak{u},\chi)$ be the subsequence and limit pair of Proposition \ref{p.eps-inner-limit}. By Proposition \ref{p.semilinear-wellposed}\ref{part.attainment}, $\mathfrak{u}$ extends to $\mathfrak{u} \in C(\overline U \times [0,\infty))$ with $\mathfrak{u} = {g}_+$ on $\partial_P U_\infty$, and $\mathfrak{u}(x,\cdot)$ is nondecreasing (resp.\ nonincreasing) in the case of strict subsolution (resp.\ supersolution) Dirichlet data. The pair $(\mathfrak{u},\chi)$ is an inner variational solution of (\ref{e.bernoulli-parabolic}) and satisfies the desired estimates by Proposition \ref{p.eps-inner-limit} \ref{part.eps-inner} and \ref{part.eps-estimates}. When $g$ is a strict subsolution, $\mathfrak{u}$ is a viscosity solution of (\ref{e.bernoulli-parabolic}) by Corollary \ref{cor:increasing}; when $g$ is a strict supersolution, $\mathfrak{u}$ is a relaxed viscosity solution by Proposition \ref{p.semilinear-limit-viscosity}.
<!-- end proof-15 -->
<!-- lemma-11: body_md -->
\label{l.subsolution-limit}
    Let $(\mathfrak u,E)$ be a bounded relaxed subsolution of \eqref{e.bernoulli-parabolic} in $U \times (0,\infty)$ such that $\mathfrak u(\cdot,t) \to u_\infty$ locally uniformly in $U$ as $t \to \infty$ and {define $$E_\infty := {\limsup_{T\to \infty}}^*\bigcap_{t\geq T}E_t.$$} Then $(u_\infty,E_\infty)$ is a relaxed subsolution of \eqref{e.bernoulli-basic} in $U$.
<!-- end lemma-11 -->
<!-- proof-16: body_md -->
{The uniform convergence of $\mathfrak{u}(\cdot,t)\to u_\infty$ ensures that $\{u_\infty > 0 \}\subset E_\infty,$ as is necessary for a relaxed solution. We now verify the necessary PDE relations.}

    Let $\varphi$ be a smooth test function touching $u_\infty$ from above in $E_\infty \cap U$ strictly at some $x_0 \in E_\infty \cap U$ {(without loss of generality, since we may perturb $\varphi$ by $C|x-x_0|^4$)}.  Then define for any $\eta>0$ and $n \in \mathbb{N}$
    \[ \psi_n(x,t) = \varphi(x) -\eta t+n\]
    Let $(x_n,t_n)$ be a first touching point where $\psi_n$ touches $\mathfrak u$ from above in $E$, i.e. 
    \[t_n = \min \{t : \text{ there is } x\in E_t \cap {\overline{U}} \hbox{ with }  \psi_n(x,t) \leq \mathfrak u(x,t)\}.\]
    Then, as long as $x_n \in U$,
    \begin{equation}\label{eqn:alt1}
    0 \geq (\partial_t-\Delta)\psi_n(x_n,t_n) = -\eta - \Delta \varphi(x_n) \ \hbox{ so } \ \Delta \varphi(x_n) \geq -\eta
    \end{equation}
    or 
    \begin{equation}\label{eqn:alt2}
    \psi(x_n,t_n) = 0  \ \hbox{ and } \ |\nabla \psi(x_n,t_n)| \geq Q(x_n),
    \end{equation}
    {since the relaxed subsolution Definition \ref{d.parabolic-relaxed-subsolution} implies the standard touching properties.}
    
     We claim now that $t_n \to \infty$ and $x_n \to x_0$ as $n \to \infty$. The first follows since $u$ is bounded and $\psi_n \to +\infty$ as $n \to \infty$ for $0 \leq t \leq T$. 
     {By hypothesis $u_\infty - \varphi$ has a strict maximum in $E_\infty \cap U $ at $x_0$ with value $0$. Perturbing $\varphi$ by $C|x-x_0|^4$, we may assume there is $r>0$ with $B_r(x_0) \subset\subset U$ such that 
     \[ x_n \in \mathop{\textup{argmax}}_{x \in {\overline{B_r(x_0)}} \cap E_{t_n}} (\mathfrak u(t_n,x)-\varphi(x))\]
     for sufficiently large $t_n.$}
      Since $x_0 \in {\limsup}^*E_{t_n}$ {by definition of $E_\infty$,} there is a sequence $E_{t_{n_j}}\ni y_{n_j} \to x_0$ and, using $\mathfrak u(t_n,\cdot) \to u_\infty$ uniformly {in $\overline{B_r(x_0)}$},
     \begin{align*}
         \limsup_{n \to \infty}(\mathfrak u(t_n,x_n)-\varphi(x_n))&= \limsup_{n \to \infty}\max_{x \in {\overline{B_r(x_0)}}\cap E_{t_n}} (\mathfrak u(t_n,x)-\varphi(x)) \\
         &\geq \limsup_{j \to \infty}(\mathfrak u(t_{n_j},y_{n_j})-\varphi(y_{n_j})) \\
         &=(u_\infty-\varphi)(x_0)= 0
     \end{align*}
     Define
     \[M_n(\rho) := \max_{(\overline{B_r} \setminus B_\rho) \cap E_{{t_n}}}(\mathfrak u(t_n,\cdot)-\varphi) \ \hbox{ and } \ M_\infty(\rho):= \max_{(\overline{B_r} \setminus B_\rho) \cap E_{\infty}}(u_\infty-\varphi).\]
     By Lemma \ref{l.limit-max}, $M_\infty(\rho) = \limsup_{n \to \infty} M_n(\rho)$. Since the maximum of $u_\infty-\varphi$ on $E$ at $x_0$ is strict, we have for all $0 < \rho \leq r$ 
     \[ 0> M_\infty(\rho) = \limsup_{n \to \infty} M_n(\rho).    \]
     Thus, by {considering a subsequence of $x_n$ (not relabeled),} we have $x_n \in \overline{B_\rho(x_0)}$ for $n$ sufficiently large. {A diagonalization argument with $\rho\to 0$ shows} $x_n \to x_0$.
    
    {Now we conclude, taking the limit in the previous inequalities \eqref{eqn:alt1} and \eqref{eqn:alt2}, that either (if the first alternative occurs infinitely often)
    \[ \Delta \varphi(x_0) \geq  -\eta\]
    or (if the second alternative occurs infinitely often) then $$0 = \psi_n(x_n,t_n) = \mathfrak u(x_n,t_n) \to u_\infty(x_0)= \varphi(x_0)$$ and $|\nabla \varphi(x_n,t_n)|=|\nabla \psi_n(x_n,t_n)| \geq Q(x_n)$, so
     \[\varphi(x_0) = 0  \ \hbox{ and } \ |\nabla \varphi(x_0)| \geq Q(x_0).\]
     Since $\eta \to 0$ was arbitrary we can conclude the viscosity subsolution condition.}
<!-- end proof-16 -->
<!-- lemma-12: body_md -->
\label{l.supersolution-limit}
    Let $\mathfrak u$ be a bounded viscosity {supersolution} of \eqref{e.bernoulli-parabolic} in $U \times (0,\infty)$ such that $\mathfrak{u}(\cdot,t) \to u_\infty$ locally uniformly in $U$ as $t \to \infty$. Then $u_\infty$ is a viscosity {supersolution} of \eqref{e.bernoulli-basic} in $U$.
<!-- end lemma-12 -->
<!-- proof-17: body_md -->
Let $\varphi$ a smooth test function touching $u_\infty$ from below strictly at some $x_0 \in U$.  Then define for any $\eta>0$ and $n \in \mathbb{N}$
    \[ \psi_n(x,t) := \varphi(x) +\eta t-n.\]
    Let $(x_n,t_n)$ be a first touching point where $\psi_n$ touches $\mathfrak u$ from below, i.e. 
    \[t_n = \min \{t : \text{ there is } x\in \overline{U} \hbox{ with }  \psi_n(x,t) \geq \mathfrak u(x,t)\}.\]
    Note that $\psi_n(x_n,t_n) = \mathfrak u(x_n,t_n)$. Then, as long as $x_n \in U$, either 
    \[0 \leq (\partial_t - \Delta)\psi_n(x_n,t_n) = \eta - \Delta \varphi(x_n) \ \hbox{ so } \ \Delta \varphi(x_n) \leq \eta\]
    or 
    \[\psi_n(x_n,t_n) = 0  \ \hbox{ and } \ |\nabla \psi_n(x_n,t_n)| \leq Q(x_n).\]
    
     We claim now that $t_n \to \infty$ and $x_n \to x_0$ as $n \to \infty$. The first is obvious since {$\mathfrak u \geq 0$}. {As in the subsolution case, we may assume there is $r>0$ with $B_r(x_0) \subset\subset U$ such that 
     \[ x_n = \mathop{\textup{argmin}}_{x \in \overline{B_r(x_0)}} (\mathfrak u(t_n,x)-\varphi(x))\]
     for sufficiently large $t_n$.}
     Since $\mathfrak u(t_n,\cdot) \to u_\infty$ uniformly in $\overline{B_r(x_0)}$ as $n \to \infty$ and since $u_\infty- \varphi$ has a strict local minimum at $x_0$, we can argue similarly to Lemma \ref{l.subsolution-limit} and conclude that $x_n \to x_0$.
     
     
     {The conclusion is now similar to the subsolution case, letting $n \to \infty$ in the supersolution inequalities for $\psi_n$ and and finally letting $\eta \to 0$.}
<!-- end proof-17 -->
<!-- corollary-4: body_md -->
\label{c.monotone-long-time}
    Let $\mathfrak u$ be a bounded viscosity subsolution of \eqref{e.bernoulli-parabolic} in $U \times (0,\infty)$ which is monotonically increasing in time and such that $\mathfrak u(\cdot,t) \nearrow u_\infty$ locally uniformly in $U$ as $t \to \infty$. Then $u_\infty$ is a viscosity subsolution of \eqref{e.bernoulli-basic} in $U$.
<!-- end corollary-4 -->
<!-- proof-18: body_md -->
Apply Lemma \ref{l.subsolution-limit} to get $(u_\infty,E_\infty)$ is a relaxed subsolution of \eqref{e.bernoulli-basic} in $U$. Since $t \mapsto \mathfrak  u(\cdot,t)$ is monotone increasing in $t$ we conclude that
    \[E_\infty ={\limsup_{T \to \infty}}^*\bigcap_{t \geq T}E_t = {\limsup_{T \to \infty}}^*\bigcap_{t \geq T}\overline{\{\mathfrak  u(\cdot,t)>0\}} \subset \overline{\bigcup_{t>0} \overline{\{\mathfrak  u(\cdot,t)>0\}}} = \overline{\{u_\infty>0\}}.\]
    So $u_\infty$ is a subsolution of \eqref{e.bernoulli-basic} in $U$.
<!-- end proof-18 -->
<!-- lemma-13: body_md -->
\label{l.subsolution-inner-limit}
    Let $(\mathfrak{u},\mathfrak{\chi})$ be an inner variational solution and viscosity supersolution of \eqref{e.bernoulli-parabolic} satisfying \eqref{eqn:diss2}--\eqref{eqn:chiEst2}. {Then there is a sequence $t\to \infty$ such that} $\mathfrak{u}(\cdot,t) \to u_\infty$ locally uniformly, $\mathfrak{\chi}(t) \to \chi_\infty$ in $L^1_{\textup{loc}}$, and $(u_\infty,\chi_\infty)$ is both an inner variational solution and a viscosity solution of \eqref{e.bernoulli-basic}.
<!-- end lemma-13 -->
<!-- proof-19: body_md -->
By Theorem \ref{t.longtime-inner} the limit $u(\cdot,t) \to u_\infty$ exists locally uniformly and in $H^1_{\rm loc}(U)$ {(without taking a subsequence)} in $U$, {$\chi(t_i)\to \chi_\infty$ in $L^1_{\textup{loc}}(U)$ for a subsequence $t_i\to \infty$,} and so $(u_\infty, {\chi_\infty})$ is an inner variational solution of \eqref{e.bernoulli-basic} by Lemma \ref{l.inner-compactness-stability}. The desired interior Lipschitz bound holds on each $V \subset\subset U$ {by passing \eqref{eqn:LipEst} to the limit.} Then Lemma \ref{l.inner-variational-implies-subsoln} implies that $u_\infty$ is a viscosity subsolution of \eqref{e.bernoulli-basic}, and Lemma \ref{l.supersolution-limit}  implies that $u_\infty$ is a viscosity supersolution of \eqref{e.bernoulli-basic}.
<!-- end proof-19 -->
<!-- proposition-6: body_md -->
\label{p.inner-smallest}
{Let ${g}$} be a smooth strict subsolution of (\ref{e.bernoulli-basic}) on $\overline{U}$ in the sense of Definition \ref{d.strict-sub} with $g|_{\partial U}>0$, and let $u$ be the smallest supersolution of (\ref{e.bernoulli-basic}) above ${g}$ in the sense of (\ref{e.perron-def-super}). Then $u$ is both an inner variational and viscosity solution of (\ref{e.bernoulli-basic}) in $U$.
<!-- end proposition-6 -->
<!-- proof-20: body_md -->
Let {$v$ be any} supersolution of \eqref{e.bernoulli-basic} in $U$ above $g_+$, i.e., $v\in S_g$ from \eqref{eqn:S_g}. Let $a_0>0$ be sufficiently small so that $g+a$ satisfies {Definition \ref{d.strict-sub}} with uniform constants when $|a| < a_0$. 



For $a_0<a<0$, by Theorem \ref{t.parabolic-existence}, there exists $\mathfrak{u}_a$ which is an inner variational and viscosity solution of the parabolic Bernoulli problem \eqref{e.bernoulli-parabolic} with $\mathfrak{u}_a(x,t) = (g(x)+a)_+$ on $\partial_P U_\infty$. Furthermore $\mathfrak{u}_a$ is monotone increasing in $t$.
Note that by assumption of $g>0$ on $\partial U$ that $\mathfrak{u}_a  = g(x)+a \prec g  \leq v$ on $\partial_P U_\infty$ (this is where we use positivity of the boundary data; see Figure \ref{fig:precFail}). Consequently, monotonicity, the comparison Theorem \ref{t.comparison}, and {Remark \ref{eqn:statToPara}}
imply
$$(g+a)_+\leq \mathfrak{u}_a \prec v \quad \text{ in } U_\infty.$$
Taking $t\to \infty$ gives that
$$(g+a)_+\leq u_{a,\infty} : = \lim_{t\to \infty}\mathfrak{u}_a(\cdot,t) \leq v \quad \text{ in } U ,$$
where by Theorem \ref{t.longtime-inner} and Corollary \ref{cor:increasing}, $u_{a,\infty}$ is both an inner variational and viscosity solution of \eqref{e.bernoulli-basic}, and in fact satisfies the Lipschitz estimate \eqref{eqn:inftyLip} and perimeter bound for its associated `positivity set' $\chi_{a,\infty}$ \eqref{eqn:inftyPerim}. Passing $a\uparrow 0,$
we have
$$g_+\leq \hat u := \lim_{a\uparrow 0} u_{a,\infty} \leq v \quad \text{ in } U ,$$
and as inner variational solutions and viscosity supersolutions are stable under uniform limits (with control on the perimeter of $\chi_{a,\infty}$), see Lemma \ref{l.inner-compactness-stability} and Lemma \ref{l.super-stability}, {$\hat u$ is both an inner variational and viscosity solution. Taking the infimum over $v\in \mathcal{S}_g$, see \eqref{e.perron-def-super}, we find $\hat u \leq u$. However, since $\hat u\in \mathcal{S}_g$, we recover $\hat u = u$ and conclude the theorem.}
<!-- end proof-20 -->
<!-- proposition-7: body_md -->
\label{p.inner-largest}
Let $U$ be a regular domain, ${g}$ be a smooth strict supersolution of (\ref{e.bernoulli-basic}) on $\overline{U}$ in the sense of Definition \ref{d.strict-sub}, and let $u$ be the largest subsolution below ${g}$ in the sense of (\ref{e.perron-def-super}). Then $u$ is both an inner variational and viscosity solution of (\ref{e.bernoulli-basic}) in $U$.
<!-- end proposition-7 -->
<!-- proof-21: body_md -->
Analogous to before, let {$v$ be any} subsolution of \eqref{e.bernoulli-basic} in $U$ below $g_+$, i.e., $v\in S^g$ from \eqref{eqn:S^g}. Let $a_0>0$ be sufficiently small so that $g+a$ satisfies {Definition \ref{d.strict-sub}} with uniform constants when $|a| < a_0$. 



For $0<a<a_0$, by Theorem \ref{t.parabolic-existence}, there exists $\mathfrak{u}^a$ which is an inner variational and viscosity solution of the parabolic Bernoulli problem \eqref{e.bernoulli-parabolic} with $\mathfrak{u}^a(x,t) = (g(x)+a)_+$ on $\partial_P( U \times (0,\infty))$. Furthermore $\mathfrak{u}^a$ is monotone decreasing in $t$.
As $v$ is \emph{below} $g_+$, we have that
$v \leq g_+ \prec (g+a)_+$ in $\overline U$, so that
$v \prec \mathfrak{u}^a$ on $\partial_P U_\infty$.
Applying monotonicity, the comparison Theorem \ref{t.comparison}, and {Remark \ref{eqn:statToPara}},
we obtain
$$v\prec \mathfrak{u}^a \leq (g+a)_+ \quad \text{ in } U_\infty,$$
and passing $t\to \infty$ gives
$$v\leq u^a_\infty : = \lim_{t\to \infty}\mathfrak{u}^a \leq (g+a)_+ \quad \text{ in } U .$$
By Theorem \ref{t.longtime-inner} and Lemma \ref{l.super-stability}, $u^a_{\infty}$ is both an inner variational and viscosity \emph{super}solution of \eqref{e.bernoulli-basic}, and satisfies the Lipschitz estimate \eqref{eqn:inftyLip} and perimeter bound for its associated `positivity set' $\chi^a_{\infty}$ \eqref{eqn:inftyPerim}. Passing $a\downarrow 0,$
we have
$$v\leq \check u := \lim_{a\downarrow 0} u^a_{\infty} \leq g_+ \quad \text{ in } U ,$$
and as inner variational solutions and viscosity supersolutions are stable under uniform limits (with control on the perimeter of $\chi_{a,\infty}$), see Lemma \ref{l.inner-compactness-stability} and Lemma \ref{l.super-stability}, we find that $\check u$ is both. Finally, we apply Theorem \ref{l.inner-variational-implies-subsoln} to conclude that $\check u$ is also a viscosity subsolution. 
As in the proof of Proposition \ref{p.inner-smallest}, a sandwiching argument gives $\check u = u,$ and concludes the theorem.
<!-- end proof-21 -->
<!-- lemma-14: body_md -->
\label{l.downward}
  If $u$ is a smallest supersolution (resp.\ largest subsolution) of \eqref{e.bernoulli-basic} in $U$ in the sense of Definition \ref{d.largest-smallest} then $u$ is a downward (resp.\ upward) minimizer of $J(\cdot ;U)$.
<!-- end lemma-14 -->
<!-- proof-22: body_md -->
\emph{Step 1: smallest supersolution case.} Condition (i) of Definition \ref{d.directional} holds as {$u$ is a viscosity solution by Proposition \ref{p.inner-smallest},} so it remains to prove the energy inequality \eqref{eqn:directionalMinimality} for downward competitors. We minimize the energy \eqref{e.energy} with $u$ as an obstacle from above: Let $B \subset \subset U$ be an open set and let $w$ be a minimizer of
   \begin{equation}\label{e.obstacle-remin}
       \min \{ {J_Q}(w;B): \ w \in u+H^1_0(B), \ 0 \leq w \leq u\},
   \end{equation}
   which exists by the direct method (the class is nonempty as $u$ belongs to it {and $J_Q$ is lower semi-continuous}). Further $w$ is continuous in $B$ by the regularity theory for such obstacle problems \cite{FeldmanKimPozar2}*{Section 3}. {We claim that
   \begin{equation}\label{eqn:equiv}
   w\equiv u
   \end{equation}
    which by definition of $w$, implies the desired downward minimality for $u$. To obtain the claim, we show $w$ is a viscosity supersolution of \eqref{e.bernoulli-basic} in $U$, and since $u$ is the smallest supersolution and $w\leq u$, this gives \eqref{eqn:equiv}.}
   
   
   To verify $w$ {(extended by $u$ outside of $B$)} is a viscosity supersolution, suppose $\varphi \in C^\infty(U)$ touches $w$ {strictly} from below at $x_0 \in U$. If $w(x_0) = u(x_0)$ then, since $w \leq u$, $\varphi$ also touches $u$ from below at $x_0$, and the supersolution property of $u$ yields the desired outcome. Otherwise $w(x_0) < u(x_0)$; since $u \equiv w$ outside of $\overline{B}$, the touching point $x_0 \in B$ and, {by continuity of the functions,} $w < u$ in a neighborhood $B_r(x_0) \subset B$. Suppose for contradiction that the supersolution condition fails at $x_0$. Then for small $\delta > 0$ the upward perturbation $w \vee (\varphi + \delta)_+$ strictly decreases the energy, by the computation of \cite{FeldmanKimPozar}*{proof of Lemma 3.3}: failure of both alternatives means $\Delta\varphi(x_0) > 0$, or $\varphi(x_0) = 0$ and $|\nabla\varphi(x_0)| > Q(x_0)$, and the energy difference formula \cite{FeldmanKimPozar}*{Lemma A.1}  shows $J(w \vee (\varphi + \delta)_+; B) < J(w;B)$ for $\delta$ small. Furthermore, for $\delta$ small the perturbation is supported in $B_r(x_0)$ and satisfies the constraint $0 \leq w \vee (\varphi + \delta)_+ \leq u$, so it is admissible in (\ref{e.obstacle-remin}). This contradicts minimality of $w$ and proves the claim.

    \emph{Step 2: largest subsolution case.} Parallel to Step 1, condition (i) of Definition \ref{d.directional} holds as {$u$ is a viscosity solution by Proposition \ref{p.inner-largest}.} To obtain directional minimality \eqref{eqn:directionalMinimality}, we minimize the energy with $u$ as an obstacle from below: let $B \subset \subset U$ and let $w$ be a minimizer of
   \begin{equation}\label{e.obstacle-remin-sub}
       \min \{ J(w;B): \ w \in u+H^1_0(B), \ w \geq u\},
   \end{equation}
   which exists and is continuous as before. As above it suffices to show $w \equiv u$ {and this follows from showing $w$ is a viscosity subsolution of \eqref{e.bernoulli-basic} in $U$.}

   To verify $w$ is a viscosity subsolution, suppose that $\varphi \in C^\infty(U)$ touches $w$ strictly from above in $\overline{\{w>0\}} \cap U$ at $x_0$. If $x_0 \in \overline{\{u>0\}}$ and $w(x_0) = u(x_0)$ then, since $w \geq u$, $\varphi_+$ also touches $u$ from above at $x_0 \in \overline{\{u>0\}}$, and the subsolution property of $u$ allows us to conclude. Otherwise either $$\text{(i)} \qquad w(x_0) > u(x_0) \geq 0,$$ or $$\text{(ii)} \qquad x_0 \not\in \overline{\{u>0\}}.$$ Since $u \equiv w$ outside of ${B}$, we have $$\text{(i)} \implies x_0 \in B$$ and $$\text{(ii)} \implies x_0 \in \overline{B}.$$ Suppose for contradiction the subsolution condition fails at $x_0$. {Applying \cite{FeldmanKimPozar}*{Lemma 3.3} once again,} the downward perturbation $w \wedge (\varphi - \delta)_+$ strictly decreases the energy for small $\delta>0$. {To obtain a contradiction with \eqref{e.obstacle-remin-sub}, the perturbation must be an admissible competitor. Precisely, it must} remain above the obstacle $u$ and only modify $w$ inside $B$, i.e., {$w \wedge (\varphi-\delta)_+ = u$ outside of $B$}. 
   
   First we show that the perturbation is above the obstacle. In case (i), $u < w \leq \varphi_+$ near $x_0$ and so by continuity $u\leq w \wedge (\varphi-\delta)_+$ near $x_0$ for small $\delta$. In case (ii), $u=0$ in a neighborhood of $x_0$ so $w \wedge (\varphi-\delta)_+ \geq 0 =u$ near $x_0$ as well.
   
   Next we show that the perturbation is supported in $B$. Since the touching is strict $\{(\varphi-\delta)_+ < w\} \subset B_{o(1)}(x_0)$ as $\delta \to 0$. So if $x_0 \in B$ {(whether in case (i) or (ii))} just choose $\delta>0$ sufficiently small so that $\{(\varphi-\delta)_+ < w\} \subset B$. If $x_0 \in \partial B$, then $w(x_0) = u(x_0)$ and we must also be in case (ii) $x_0 \not\in \overline{\{u>0\}}$. Consequently, $u \equiv 0 $ in a small ball $B_r(x_0)$ and $w(x_0) = u(x_0) = 0$. since $w = u$ outside $B$, we get $w \equiv 0$ in $B_r(x_0) \setminus B$. Choosing $\delta>0$ small enough that $\{(\varphi - \delta)_+ < w\} \subset B_r(x_0)$ (possible again by the strict touching), we conclude $w \wedge (\varphi - \delta)_+ = 0 = w = u$ in $B_r(x_0) \setminus B$, and therefore the perturbation is supported in $B$. Thus it is a valid competitor for (\ref{e.obstacle-remin-sub}), providing a contradiction.
<!-- end proof-22 -->
<!-- head-14: body_md -->
Condition (i) of Definition \ref{d.directional} holds as {$u$ is a viscosity solution by Proposition \ref{p.inner-smallest},} so it remains to prove the energy inequality \eqref{eqn:directionalMinimality} for downward competitors. We minimize the energy \eqref{e.energy} with $u$ as an obstacle from above: Let $B \subset \subset U$ be an open set and let $w$ be a minimizer of
   \begin{equation}\label{e.obstacle-remin}
       \min \{ {J_Q}(w;B): \ w \in u+H^1_0(B), \ 0 \leq w \leq u\},
   \end{equation}
   which exists by the direct method (the class is nonempty as $u$ belongs to it {and $J_Q$ is lower semi-continuous}). Further $w$ is continuous in $B$ by the regularity theory for such obstacle problems \cite{FeldmanKimPozar2}*{Section 3}. {We claim that
   \begin{equation}\label{eqn:equiv}
   w\equiv u
   \end{equation}
    which by definition of $w$, implies the desired downward minimality for $u$. To obtain the claim, we show $w$ is a viscosity supersolution of \eqref{e.bernoulli-basic} in $U$, and since $u$ is the smallest supersolution and $w\leq u$, this gives \eqref{eqn:equiv}.}
<!-- end head-14 -->
<!-- head-15: body_md -->
Parallel to Step 1, condition (i) of Definition \ref{d.directional} holds as {$u$ is a viscosity solution by Proposition \ref{p.inner-largest}.} To obtain directional minimality \eqref{eqn:directionalMinimality}, we minimize the energy with $u$ as an obstacle from below: let $B \subset \subset U$ and let $w$ be a minimizer of
   \begin{equation}\label{e.obstacle-remin-sub}
       \min \{ J(w;B): \ w \in u+H^1_0(B), \ w \geq u\},
   \end{equation}
   which exists and is continuous as before. As above it suffices to show $w \equiv u$ {and this follows from showing $w$ is a viscosity subsolution of \eqref{e.bernoulli-basic} in $U$.}
<!-- end head-15 -->
<!-- lemma-15: body_md -->
\label{l.monotone}
Assume that $g_\varepsilon$ is a continuous subsolution (resp. supersolution) of \eqref{e.bernoulli-parabolic-semilinear}. Then the unique classical solution $\mathfrak{u}_\varepsilon$ of \eqref{e.bernoulli-parabolic-semilinear} is monotone increasing (resp. monotone decreasing) in $t$.
<!-- end lemma-15 -->
<!-- proof-23: body_md -->
By comparison $\mathfrak{u}_\varepsilon(x,h) \geq g_\varepsilon(x)$ for all $h >0$. Then consider $\mathfrak{u}_\varepsilon(x,t+h)$, which also solves \eqref{e.bernoulli-parabolic-semilinear} with initial data $\mathfrak{u}_\varepsilon(x,h) \geq g_\varepsilon(x)$ and lateral boundary data $g_\varepsilon(x)$. In other words it is a supersolution of \eqref{e.bernoulli-parabolic-semilinear} so by comparison $\mathfrak{u}_\varepsilon(x,t+h) \geq \mathfrak{u}_\varepsilon(x,t)$ for all $t>0$. Since $h>0$ was arbitrary we derive the monotonicity property. The case of supersolution initial data is symmetrical.
<!-- end proof-23 -->
<!-- lemma-16: body_md -->
\label{l.profile-sub}
   For each $\theta \in (0,1)$ there is $\Phi = \Phi_{1,\theta} \in C^\infty(\mathbb{R})$ with the following properties.
\begin{enumerate}[label = (\roman*)]
    \item\label{part.profile-sub-a} $(\Phi)'' = \theta \beta(\Phi)$ on $\mathbb{R}$.
    \item\label{part.profile-sub-b} $\sqrt{1-\theta} \leq (\Phi)' \leq 1$ on $\mathbb{R}$, and $\Phi(s) = s$ for $s \geq 1$.
    \item\label{part.profile-sub-c} There is $s_0 \in [-c_\theta, 0]$, with $c_\theta := \frac{1-\sqrt{1-\theta}}{\sqrt{1-\theta}}$, such that $\Phi(s_0) = 0$ and $\Phi > 0$ exactly on $(s_0,\infty)$. Moreover $s \leq \Phi(s) \leq 1$ for all $s \leq 1$, and $\sup_{\mathbb{R}} |(\Phi)_+ - s_+| \leq 1$.
\end{enumerate}
<!-- end lemma-16 -->
<!-- proof-24: body_md -->
Since $0 \leq 2\mathcal{B} \leq 1$, the function
\[G(z) := \int_1^z \frac{dw}{\sqrt{(1-\theta) + 2\theta  \mathcal{B}(w)}}\]
is well defined for $z \in \mathbb{R}$, is $C^1$ with $G' \in [1, (1-\theta)^{-1/2}]$, and is therefore a bijection of $\mathbb{R}$ onto $\mathbb{R}$. Define $\Phi(s) := G^{-1}(s - 1)$. Then $\Phi(1) = 1$ and
\begin{equation}\label{e.profile-foc}
(\Phi)'(s) = \sqrt{(1-\theta) + 2\theta  \mathcal{B}(\Phi(s))} \in [\sqrt{1-\theta},  1].
\end{equation}
Differentiating (\ref{e.profile-foc}) and using $\mathcal{B}' = \beta$ gives $(\Phi)'' = \theta \beta(\Phi)$, and since $\beta \in C^\infty$ a bootstrap of this identity gives $\Phi \in C^\infty(\mathbb{R})$. For $s \geq 1$ we have $\Phi(s) \geq 1$ (as $(\Phi)' > 0$), hence $\mathcal{B}(\Phi(s)) = \tfrac12$, hence $(\Phi)' = 1$, and with $\Phi(1)=1$ this gives $\Phi(s) = s$, proving  \ref{part.profile-sub-b}.

For  \ref{part.profile-sub-c}: the function $s \mapsto s - \Phi(s)$ is nondecreasing by (\ref{e.profile-foc}) and vanishes at $s = 1$, so $\Phi(s) \geq s$ for $s \leq 1$; also $\Phi(s) \leq \Phi(1) = 1$ for $s \leq 1$ since $(\Phi)' > 0$. In particular $\Phi(0) \geq 0$, so the unique zero $s_0$ of the strictly increasing function $\Phi$ satisfies $s_0 \leq 0$. On $[0,1]$, $(\Phi)' \geq \sqrt{1-\theta}$ gives $\Phi(0) \leq \Phi(1) - \sqrt{1-\theta} = 1 - \sqrt{1-\theta}$, and then $(\Phi)' \geq \sqrt{1-\theta}$ on $[s_0, 0]$ gives $|s_0| \leq \Phi(0)/\sqrt{1-\theta} \leq c_\theta$. Finally, for $s \geq 1$ we have $(\Phi(s))_+ - s_+ = 0$; for $s_0 \leq s \leq 1$ both $(\Phi(s))_+$ and $s_+$ lie in $[0,1]$; and for $s \leq s_0$ both terms vanish since $s \leq s_0 \leq 0$. This proves  \ref{part.profile-sub-c}.
<!-- end proof-24 -->
<!-- lemma-17: body_md -->
\label{l.profile-super}
    For each $\hat\theta \in (1,\infty)$ there are a constant level $\kappa = \kappa_{\hat\theta} \in (0,1)$ and constants $C_{\hat\theta} \geq 1 \geq c_{\hat\theta} > 0$, all depending only on $\hat\theta$ and $\beta$, and $\Psi = \Psi_{1,\hat\theta} \in C^\infty(\mathbb{R})$ with the following properties.
\begin{enumerate}[label = (\roman*)]
    \item\label{part.profile-super-a} $0 \leq (\Psi)'' \leq \hat\theta  \beta(\Psi)$ on $\mathbb{R}$.
    \item\label{part.profile-super-b} $0 < (\Psi)' \leq 1$ on $\mathbb{R}$, and $\Psi(s) = s$ for $s \geq 1$.
    \item\label{part.profile-super-c} $\max(s,\kappa) < \Psi(s) < 1$ for all $s < 1$, and $\Psi(s) \downarrow \kappa$ as $s \to -\infty$. In particular $\Psi > \kappa > 0$ on $\mathbb{R}$ and $\sup_{\mathbb{R}}|\Psi - s_+| \leq 1$.
    \item\label{part.profile-super-e} $\max\{\Psi(s) - \kappa ,(\Psi)'(s) , (\Psi)''(s)\} \leq C_{\hat\theta}  e^{c_{\hat\theta}  s}$ for all $s \leq 0$.
\end{enumerate}
<!-- end lemma-17 -->
<!-- proof-25: body_md -->
Set $\tilde\theta := \tfrac{1+\hat\theta}{2} \in (1,\hat\theta)$ and $\sigma := \hat\theta/\tilde\theta - 1 > 0$. Since $\beta > 0$ on $(0,1)$, $2\mathcal{B}$ is a strictly increasing bijection from $[0,1]$ onto $[0,1]$, so there is a unique $\kappa = \kappa_{\hat\theta} \in (0,1)$ with
\begin{equation}\label{e.kappa-def}
2\mathcal{B}(\kappa) = \frac{\tilde\theta - 1}{\tilde\theta} .
\end{equation}
Note that $\kappa \to 1$ as $\hat \theta \to \infty$. Define $P : [\kappa,\infty) \to [0,1]$ by $P(z) := 2\tilde\theta\big(\mathcal{B}(z) - \mathcal{B}(\kappa)\big)$. Then $P$ is smooth and nondecreasing with $P' = 2\tilde\theta\beta \geq 0$, strictly increasing on $[\kappa,1]$, $P(\kappa) = 0$, $P'(\kappa) = 2\tilde\theta\beta(\kappa) > 0$, and
\[P(z) = 2\tilde\theta\Big(\tfrac12 - \tfrac{\tilde\theta-1}{2\tilde\theta}\Big) = 1 \  \hbox{for } z \geq 1 .\]

It would be natural to solve $\Psi' = \sqrt{P(\Psi)}$ with $\Psi(1) = 1$ since then $\Psi'' = \tilde\theta \beta(\Psi)$, but this solution attaches to the level $\kappa$ at some finite value and is only $C^{1,1}$ at the attachment point. To get a smooth solution we instead we flatten the vector field quadratically at the bottom of its range, spending the slack $\sigma$. 

Fix a smooth reparametrization $\eta \in C^\infty([0,1];[0,1])$, depending only on $\sigma$, with
\begin{equation}\label{e.eta-properties}
\eta(p) = p^2 \ \hbox{ on } [0,p_0], \  \eta(p) = p \ \hbox{ on } [p_1,1], \  0 < \eta(p) \leq p \ \hbox{ on } (0,1], \  0 \leq \eta' \leq 1+\sigma,
\end{equation}
for suitable $0 < p_0 < p_1 < 1$.


Define $g : [\kappa,\infty) \to [0,1]$ by $g(z) := \sqrt{\eta(P(z))}$. The function $g$ is smooth: near $z = \kappa$ we have $P(z) \leq p_0$, so $g = P$ there, which is smooth; and where $P > 0$ the composition $\eta(P)$ is smooth and positive (by (\ref{e.eta-properties})), so its square root is smooth. Moreover:
\begin{enumerate}[label = (\alph*)]
\item\label{it.g-ineq} $0 \leq (g^2)'(z) = \eta'(P(z)) P'(z) \leq (1+\sigma)\cdot 2\tilde\theta\beta(z) = 2\hat\theta \beta(z)$ for all $z \geq \kappa$;
\item\label{it.g-firstint} $g(z)^2 = \eta(P(z)) \leq P(z)$, so in particular $g \leq 1$, with $g(z) = 1$ for $z \geq 1$ and $g(z) < 1$ for $z < 1$ (as $P < 1$ there);
\item\label{it.g-linear} $g(\kappa) = 0$, $g > 0$ on $(\kappa,\infty)$, and, with $z_0 \in (\kappa,1)$ defined by $P(z_0) = p_0$,
\[c_1 (z-\kappa) \leq g(z) = P(z) \leq c_2 (z-\kappa) \  \hbox{for } z \in [\kappa, z_0],\]
where $c_1 := 2\tilde\theta\min_{[\kappa,z_0]}\beta > 0$ and $c_2 := 2\tilde\theta \max\beta$.
\end{enumerate}
Let $\Psi$ be the maximal solution of the autonomous ODE
\[(\Psi)' = g(\Psi), \  \Psi(1) = 1 .\]
Since $g$ is locally Lipschitz and $z \equiv \kappa$ is a stationary solution, $\Psi$ is defined on all of $\mathbb{R}$, takes values in $(\kappa,\infty)$, and is strictly increasing. Bootstrapping the ODE with $g$ smooth gives $\Psi \in C^\infty(\mathbb{R})$. For $s \geq 1$, $g(\Psi) = 1$ once $\Psi \geq 1$, so $\Psi(s) = s$. This and $0 < (\Psi)' = g(\Psi) \leq 1$ prove  \ref{part.profile-super-b}. Differentiating,
\[(\Psi)'' = g'(\Psi)  g(\Psi) = \tfrac12 (g^2)'(\Psi) \in \big[0,\ \hat\theta \beta(\Psi)\big]\]
by \ref{it.g-ineq}, which proves \ref{part.profile-super-a}. 


For  \ref{part.profile-super-c}: $\Psi > \kappa$ and $\Psi(s) < \Psi(1) = 1$ for $s < 1$ by strict monotonicity. The function $s - \Psi(s)$ has derivative $1 - g(\Psi(s)) > 0$ for $s < 1$ by \ref{it.g-firstint} and vanishes at $s = 1$, so $\Psi(s) > s$ for $s < 1$. As $s \to -\infty$, $\Psi$ decreases to a limit $\ell \geq \kappa$ which must satisfy $g(\ell) = 0$, so $\ell = \kappa$. The bound $\sup_\mathbb{R}|\Psi - s_+| \leq 1$ follows since for $s \leq 1$ both $\Psi(s)$ and $s_+$ lie in $[0,1]$, while for $s \geq 1$ they are equal.

For \ref{part.profile-super-c}: let $s_\# \in \mathbb{R}$ be the time with $\Psi(s_\#) = z_0$ (with $z_0$ from \ref{it.g-linear}). For $s \leq s_\#$ we have $\Psi(s) \in (\kappa, z_0]$, where \ref{it.g-linear} gives $\frac{d}{ds}\log(\Psi - \kappa) = \frac{g(\Psi)}{\Psi - \kappa} \geq c_1$. Integrating from $s$ to $s_\#$,
\[\Psi(s) - \kappa \leq (z_0 - \kappa)  e^{c_1 (s - s_\#)} \leq e^{c_1|s_\#|}  e^{c_1 s} \  \hbox{for } s \leq s_\#,\]
while for $s_\# \leq s \leq 0$ (if this interval is nonempty) the trivial bound $\Psi(s) - \kappa \leq 1 \leq e^{c_1|s_\#|}e^{c_1 s}$ holds. On the same regions, $(\Psi)' = g(\Psi) \leq c_2(\Psi - \kappa)$ for $s \leq s_\#$ and $(\Psi)' \leq 1$ otherwise, and $(\Psi)'' = \tfrac12\eta'(P)P'(\Psi) \leq P(\Psi)\cdot 2\tilde\theta\max\beta \leq c_2^2(\Psi-\kappa)$ for $s \leq s_\#$ (using $\eta' \leq 2P$ on $[0,p_0]$) and $(\Psi)'' \leq \hat\theta\max\beta$ otherwise. Since $s_\#$, $c_1$, $c_2$, $z_0$ depend only on $\hat\theta$ and $\beta$, all three bounds combine into \ref{part.profile-super-c} with $c_{\hat\theta} := c_1$ and a suitable $C_{\hat\theta} = C_{\hat\theta}(\hat\theta,\beta)$.
<!-- end proof-25 -->
<!-- lemma-18: body_md -->
\label{l.well-prepared}
Assume that $g$ is a smooth strict subsolution (resp. smooth strict supersolution) of \eqref{e.bernoulli-basic} in the sense of \ref{d.strict-sub} with parameters $\delta_0,a_0>0$. Define $\theta = \frac{1}{1+\delta_0}$, $\hat \theta = \frac{1}{1-\delta_0}$, and
\[g_\varepsilon := \big(\Phi_{\varepsilon,\theta}({g})\big)_+ \  \Big(\hbox{resp. } g_\varepsilon := \Psi_{\varepsilon,\hat\theta}({g})\Big).\]
 There is $\varepsilon_0 = \varepsilon_0 > 0$ depending on $(a_0,\delta_0,Q_{\min},Q_{\max},\beta,\|{g}\|_{C^2(\overline U)})$ such that for every $\varepsilon \in (0,\varepsilon_0]$ the following hold.
\begin{enumerate}[label = (\roman*)]
    \item\label{part.gep-1} $g_\varepsilon \in C^{0,1}(\overline{U})$ with $\|\nabla g_\varepsilon\|_{L^\infty(U)} \leq \|\nabla {g}\|_{L^\infty(U)}$, and $g_\varepsilon = {g}$ on $\{{g} \geq \varepsilon\}$.
    \item\label{part.gep-2} ${g}_+ \leq g_\varepsilon \leq {g}_+ + \varepsilon$ on $\overline{U}$.
    \item\label{part.gep-3} $g_\varepsilon$ is a viscosity subsolution (resp. classical supersolution) of the stationary equation
    \[\Delta v = Q(x)^2 \beta_\varepsilon(v) \  \hbox{in } U.\]
    \item\label{part.gep-4} With $\chi^0_\varepsilon := 2\mathcal{B}_\varepsilon(g_\varepsilon)$,
    \[J(g_\varepsilon, \chi^0_\varepsilon; U) \leq \int_U |\nabla {g}|^2   dx + Q_{\max}^2  |U| =: E_0.\]
    \item\label{part.gep-5}  In the subsolution case, $\{g_\varepsilon > 0\} = \{{g} > \varepsilon s_0\}$ with $\varepsilon s_0 \in [-c_\theta \varepsilon,  0]$ the zero of $\Phi_{\varepsilon,\theta}$. In particular
    \[\{{g} > 0\} \subset \{g_\varepsilon > 0\} \subset \{{g} > -c_\theta  \varepsilon\}.\]
\end{enumerate}
<!-- end lemma-18 -->
<!-- proof-26: body_md -->
Set $L := \|\nabla{g}\|_{L^\infty(U)}$ and $D := \|\Delta{g}\|_{L^\infty(U)}$. We first require $\varepsilon_0 \leq \tfrac{a_0}{1 + c_\theta}$, so that in the increasing case the transition region of the profile is contained in $\{|{g}| \leq a_0\}$, as quantified below.  

\emph{Subsolution case.} Write $\Phi := \Phi_{\varepsilon,\theta}$ and recall from Lemma \ref{l.profile-sub}\ref{part.profile-sub-c} the zero $\varepsilon s_0 \in [-c_\theta\varepsilon, 0]$ of $\Phi$. Item \ref{part.gep-1} holds since $0 \leq \Phi' \leq 1$ and ${g} \in C^{0,1}$, with $g_\varepsilon = (\Phi({g}))_+ = \Phi({g}) = {g}$ on $\{{g} \geq \varepsilon\}$. Item \ref{part.gep-2}: $\Phi(s) \geq s$ for all $s$ gives $(\Phi({g}))_+ \geq {g}_+$, and $\sup_\mathbb{R}|\Phi_+ - s_+| \leq \varepsilon$ gives the upper bound. Item \ref{part.gep-5} is immediate from the strict monotonicity of $\Phi$ and $\{\Phi > 0\} = (\varepsilon s_0,\infty)$. Item \ref{part.gep-4} follows from \ref{part.gep-1} and $0 \leq \chi^0_\varepsilon \leq 1$:
\[J(g_\varepsilon,\chi^0_\varepsilon;U) \leq \int_U |\nabla {g}|^2 {\bf 1}_{\{g_\varepsilon>0\}}   dx + \int_U Q(x)^2   dx \leq \int_U |\nabla{g}|^2   dx + Q_{\max}^2 |U|.\]

We prove \ref{part.gep-3}. Let $\psi \in C^2(U)$ touch $g_\varepsilon$ from above at $x_* \in U$; we must show $\Delta \psi(x_*) \geq Q(x_*)^2 \beta_\varepsilon(g_\varepsilon(x_*))$.

First suppose $g_\varepsilon(x_*) = 0$. Then $\psi \geq g_\varepsilon \geq 0$ near $x_*$ and $\psi(x_*) = 0$, so $x_*$ is a local minimum of $\psi$ and $\Delta \psi(x_*) \geq 0 = Q(x_*)^2\beta_\varepsilon(0)$, where $\beta_\varepsilon(0) = 0$ since $\operatorname{supp}\beta = [0,1]$ and $\beta$ is continuous.

Now suppose $g_\varepsilon(x_*) > 0$, i.e.\ ${g}(x_*) > \varepsilon s_0$. Near $x_*$ we have $g_\varepsilon = \Phi({g}) \in C^2$, so it suffices to verify the classical inequality at $x_*$:
\begin{equation}\label{e.chain-sub}
\Delta\big(\Phi({g})\big)(x_*) = \Phi''({g}) |\nabla{g}|^2 + \Phi'({g}) \Delta{g} \geq Q(x_*)^2\beta_\varepsilon\big(\Phi({g}(x_*))\big).
\end{equation}
Since ${g}(x_*) > \varepsilon s_0 \geq -c_\theta\varepsilon \geq -a_0$, the strict subsolution property gives $\Delta {g}(x_*) \geq 0$, and $\Phi' > 0$, so the second term in (\ref{e.chain-sub}) is non-negative. If $\beta_\varepsilon(\Phi({g}(x_*))) = 0$ then (\ref{e.chain-sub}) follows since $\Phi'' = \theta\beta_\varepsilon(\Phi) = 0$ there. If $\beta_\varepsilon(\Phi({g}(x_*))) > 0$ then $0 < \Phi({g}(x_*)) < \varepsilon$, which by Lemma \ref{l.profile-sub}\ref{part.profile-sub-c} forces $\varepsilon s_0 < {g}(x_*) < \varepsilon$, hence $|{g}(x_*)| \leq a_0$ by the choice of $\varepsilon_0$. Then the strict subsolution property gives $|\nabla {g}(x_*)|^2 \geq (1+\delta_0) Q(x_*)^2 $, and, using $\Phi'' = \theta\beta_\varepsilon(\Phi)$ and the monotonicity of $t \mapsto \frac{t}{t + \delta_0}$,
\begin{align*}
    \Phi''({g})|\nabla{g}|^2 &\geq \theta (1+\delta_0) Q(x_*)^2 \beta_\varepsilon(\Phi({g})) \geq Q(x_*)^2 \beta_\varepsilon(\Phi({g}))
\end{align*}
at $x_*$, using the definition of $\theta$ for the second inequality. This proves (\ref{e.chain-sub}), hence \ref{part.gep-3}.

\emph{Supersolution case.} Write $\Psi := \Psi_{\varepsilon,\hat\theta}$ and $\kappa := \kappa_{\hat\theta} \in (0,1)$ from Lemma \ref{l.profile-super}. Item \ref{part.gep-1} holds since $0 < \Psi' \leq 1$, with $g_\varepsilon = \Psi({g}) = {g}$ on $\{{g} \geq \varepsilon\}$. Item \ref{part.gep-2}: $\Psi(s) \geq s$ and $\Psi > 0$ give $\Psi(s) \geq s_+$, hence $\Psi({g}) \geq {g}_+$, and $\sup_\mathbb{R}|\Psi - s_+| \leq \varepsilon$ gives the upper bound. Item \ref{part.gep-5} is $\Psi > \varepsilon\kappa$. Item \ref{part.gep-4} follows as before.

For \ref{part.gep-3}, since $\Psi \in C^\infty(\mathbb{R})$ by Lemma \ref{l.profile-sub} and ${g} \in C^2(\overline U)$, the composition $g_\varepsilon = \Psi({g})$ belongs to $C^2(\overline U)$ and the supersolution property is the classical pointwise inequality
\begin{equation}\label{e.chain-super-goal}
\Delta\big(\Psi({g})\big) = \Psi''({g}) |\nabla{g}|^2 + \Psi'({g}) \Delta{g} \leq Q(x)^2\beta_\varepsilon\big(\Psi({g})\big) \  \hbox{in } U,
\end{equation}
which we verify in three regions.

Case ${g}(x) \geq \varepsilon$. Then $\Psi({g}) = {g} \geq \varepsilon$ at $x$, so $\beta_\varepsilon(\Psi({g})) = 0$ and $\Psi''({g}) = 0$ (as $\Psi$ is affine on $[\varepsilon,\infty)$), while $\Delta{g}(x) \leq 0$ since $g$ is a strict supersolution  as in Definition \ref{d.strict-sub} (as ${g}(x) \geq \varepsilon > -a_0$). Hence the left side of (\ref{e.chain-super-goal}) is non-positive.

Case $-a_0 \leq {g}(x) < \varepsilon$. Then $|{g}(x)| \leq a_0$ (using $\varepsilon \leq a_0$), so the strict supersolution property of $g$ Definition \ref{d.strict-sub} gives $\Delta {g}(x) \leq 0$ and $|\nabla{g}(x)|^2 \leq Q(x)^2 - \delta_0$. Then, using $0 \leq \Psi'' \leq \hat\theta\beta_\varepsilon(\Psi)$ from Lemma \ref{l.profile-super}\ref{part.profile-super-a} and the definition of $\hat\theta$,
\begin{align*}
    \Psi''({g})|\nabla{g}|^2 &\leq \hat\theta(1-\delta_0)Q(x)^2\beta_\varepsilon(\Psi({g})) = Q(x)^2\beta_\varepsilon(\Psi({g})).
\end{align*}
 Also $\Psi'\Delta{g} \leq 0$ since $\Delta g \leq 0$ on $g(x) \geq - a_0$. Thus, again, we have derived (\ref{e.chain-super-goal}).

Case ${g}(x) < -a_0$. Here the strict supersolution property of $g$ gives no information, and we use the exponential decay of the profile instead. By Lemma \ref{l.profile-super}\ref{part.profile-super-e},
\[\Psi''({g})|\nabla{g}|^2 + \Psi'({g})\Delta{g} \leq \frac{C_{\hat\theta}}{\varepsilon} e^{-c_{\hat\theta}a_0/\varepsilon} \big(L^2 + \varepsilon D\big) \leq \frac{C_{\hat\theta}(L^2 + D)}{\varepsilon} e^{-c_{\hat\theta} a_0/\varepsilon} .\]
On the other hand $\Psi({g}(x))/\varepsilon = \Psi({g}(x)/\varepsilon) \in \big(\kappa,\ \Psi(-a_0/\varepsilon)\big]$, and by Lemma \ref{l.profile-super}\ref{part.profile-super-c}, $\Psi(-a_0/\varepsilon) \leq \kappa + C_{\hat\theta}e^{-c_{\hat\theta}a_0/\varepsilon} \leq \tfrac{1+\kappa}{2}$ once $\varepsilon$ is small enough that $C_{\hat\theta}e^{-c_{\hat\theta}a_0/\varepsilon} \leq \tfrac{1-\kappa}{2}$. Hence, with $b_{\hat\theta} := \min_{[\kappa, \frac{1+\kappa}{2}]}\beta > 0$,
\[Q(x)^2\beta_\varepsilon\big(\Psi({g}(x))\big) = \frac{Q(x)^2}{\varepsilon}\beta\Big(\frac{\Psi({g}(x))}{\varepsilon}\Big) \geq \frac{Q_{\min}^2 b_{\hat\theta}}{\varepsilon},\]
and (\ref{e.chain-super-goal}) holds in this region as soon as $C_{\hat\theta}(L^2 + D) e^{-c_{\hat\theta}a_0/\varepsilon} \leq Q_{\min}^2 b_{\hat\theta}$. Together with the condition of the previous display this fixes the threshold $\varepsilon_0$, with the stated dependencies.
<!-- end proof-26 -->
<!-- head-16: body_md -->
Write $\Phi := \Phi_{\varepsilon,\theta}$ and recall from Lemma \ref{l.profile-sub}\ref{part.profile-sub-c} the zero $\varepsilon s_0 \in [-c_\theta\varepsilon, 0]$ of $\Phi$. Item \ref{part.gep-1} holds since $0 \leq \Phi' \leq 1$ and ${g} \in C^{0,1}$, with $g_\varepsilon = (\Phi({g}))_+ = \Phi({g}) = {g}$ on $\{{g} \geq \varepsilon\}$. Item \ref{part.gep-2}: $\Phi(s) \geq s$ for all $s$ gives $(\Phi({g}))_+ \geq {g}_+$, and $\sup_\mathbb{R}|\Phi_+ - s_+| \leq \varepsilon$ gives the upper bound. Item \ref{part.gep-5} is immediate from the strict monotonicity of $\Phi$ and $\{\Phi > 0\} = (\varepsilon s_0,\infty)$. Item \ref{part.gep-4} follows from \ref{part.gep-1} and $0 \leq \chi^0_\varepsilon \leq 1$:
\[J(g_\varepsilon,\chi^0_\varepsilon;U) \leq \int_U |\nabla {g}|^2 {\bf 1}_{\{g_\varepsilon>0\}}   dx + \int_U Q(x)^2   dx \leq \int_U |\nabla{g}|^2   dx + Q_{\max}^2 |U|.\]
<!-- end head-16 -->
<!-- head-17: body_md -->
Write $\Psi := \Psi_{\varepsilon,\hat\theta}$ and $\kappa := \kappa_{\hat\theta} \in (0,1)$ from Lemma \ref{l.profile-super}. Item \ref{part.gep-1} holds since $0 < \Psi' \leq 1$, with $g_\varepsilon = \Psi({g}) = {g}$ on $\{{g} \geq \varepsilon\}$. Item \ref{part.gep-2}: $\Psi(s) \geq s$ and $\Psi > 0$ give $\Psi(s) \geq s_+$, hence $\Psi({g}) \geq {g}_+$, and $\sup_\mathbb{R}|\Psi - s_+| \leq \varepsilon$ gives the upper bound. Item \ref{part.gep-5} is $\Psi > \varepsilon\kappa$. Item \ref{part.gep-4} follows as before.
<!-- end head-17 -->
<!-- proposition-8: body_md -->
Let $0 < r \leq 1$ and let $\mathfrak{u}_\varepsilon \geq 0$ be a classical solution of 
\[(\partial_t - \Delta)\mathfrak{u}_\varepsilon = - Q(x)\beta_\varepsilon(\mathfrak{u}_{\varepsilon}) \ \hbox{ in } \ Q_{2r}\] and continuous on $\overline{Q_{2r}}$. Then
	\begin{equation}\nonumber
	\|\nabla \mathfrak{u}_\varepsilon\|_{L^\infty(Q_r)} \leq C \left(\frac{\|\mathfrak{u}_\varepsilon\|_{L^\infty(Q_{2r})}}{r} + 1\right)
	\end{equation}
	with $C = C(d, Q_{\min}, Q_{\max}, \|\nabla(Q^2)\|_{L^\infty}, \|\beta\|_{C^1})$.
<!-- end proposition-8 -->
<!-- proposition-9: body_md -->
\label{p.localLip-initial-data}
 Let $0 < r \leq 1$ and let $\mathfrak{u}_\varepsilon \geq 0$ be a classical solution of 
\[(\partial_t - \Delta)\mathfrak{u}_\varepsilon = - Q(x)\beta_\varepsilon(\mathfrak{u}_{\varepsilon}) \ \hbox{ in } \ B_{2r} \times (0,T]\]   for some $0 < T \leq 4r^2$ and $u$ and $\nabla u$ are continuous on $\overline{B_{2r}} \times [0,T]$. Then
	\begin{equation}\nonumber
	\|\nabla \mathfrak{u}_\varepsilon\|_{L^\infty(B_r \times [0,T])} \leq C\left(\|\nabla \mathfrak{u}_\varepsilon(\cdot,0)\|_{L^\infty(B_{2r})}+\frac{\|\mathfrak{u}_\varepsilon\|_{L^\infty(B_{2r}\times[0,T])}}{r}+1\right)
	\end{equation}
	with $C = C(d, Q_{\min}, Q_{\max}, \|\nabla(Q^2)\|_{L^\infty}, \|\beta\|_{C^1})$.
<!-- end proposition-9 -->
<!-- lemma-19: body_md -->
Let $g_\varepsilon$ non-negative and Lipschitz on $\overline{U}$. Let $\mathfrak{u}_\varepsilon$ be the solution of \eqref{e.bernoulli-parabolic-semilinear}. For every $V \subset\subset U$ there is $C_V$ so that
\[\sup_{0 < \varepsilon \leq 1}\ \sup_{t > 0}\ \|\nabla \mathfrak{u}_\varepsilon(\cdot,t)\|_{L^\infty(V)} \leq C_V(1+\|g_\varepsilon\|_{L^\infty(U)}+\|\nabla g_\varepsilon\|_{L^\infty(U)}) .\]
Here $C_V $ depends only on $d(V,\mathbb{R}^d \setminus U)$, $N$, $C_\beta$, $d$, $Q_{\min}$ and $Q_{\max}$.
<!-- end lemma-19 -->
<!-- proof-27: body_md -->
By a mollification argument using the uniqueness of continuous viscosity solutions of \eqref{e.bernoulli-parabolic-semilinear} it suffices to consider the case $g_\varepsilon$ is smooth, so that $\nabla \mathfrak{u}_\varepsilon$ is continuous at $t=0$ on $V$.

Call $r = d(V,\mathbb{R}^d \setminus U)$. Let $(x,t) \in V \times (0,\infty)$. If $t \geq 4r^2$ then $Q_{2r}(x,t) \subset U_\infty$ and Proposition \ref{p.localLip} gives $|\nabla \mathfrak{u}_\varepsilon(x,t)| \leq C(\|g_\varepsilon\|_\infty/r + 1)$. If $0 < t < 4r^2$ we apply Proposition \ref{p.localLip-initial-data} and get $|\nabla \mathfrak{u}_\varepsilon(x,t)| \leq C(\|\nabla g_\varepsilon\|_\infty +\|g_\varepsilon\|_\infty/r+ 1)$.
<!-- end proof-27 -->
<!-- proof-28: body_md -->
We can assume that $Q$ is smooth so that $\mathfrak{u}_\varepsilon$ is smooth on the interior to justify all the derivative computations below, the end estimate will only depend on the Lipschitz norm of $Q$ so we can derive the general Lipschitz case by approximation. By parabolic rescaling it suffices to prove the estimate at unit scale. For $r \leq 1$ then $\hat u(y,s) := r^{-1}\mathfrak{u}_\varepsilon(x_0 + ry, t_0 + r^2 s)$ solves the same equation on $\Gamma := B_2 \times (-4,0]$ with $\hat\varepsilon := \varepsilon/r$ (note $r\beta_\varepsilon(r z) = \beta_{\varepsilon/r}(z)$) and $\hat Q(y) := Q(x_0 + ry)$ in place of $\varepsilon$ and $Q$. Then $\|\nabla(\hat Q^2)\|_\infty = r\|\nabla(Q^2)\|_\infty \leq N_Q$ since $r \leq 1$. Likewise the scaling $u \mapsto u/Q_{\max}$, $\varepsilon \mapsto \varepsilon/Q_{\max}$, $Q \mapsto Q/Q_{\max}$ maps solutions to solutions, so we may normalize $Q_{\max} = 1$.  Note that due to the former scaling argument we must handle all $ \varepsilon >0$, for now we assume that $\varepsilon \leq 1$, the case $\varepsilon \geq 1$ is easier and done at the end.

Note that in the case of Proposition \ref{p.localLip-initial-data} the rescaled domain is $\Gamma := B_2 \times (-\tau_0,0]$ for  $\tau_0 = \frac{T}{r^2} \in (0,4]$.

Call $M:= \|u\|_{L^\infty(Q_2)}$ and $L= \|\nabla u(\cdot,-\tau_0)\|_{L^\infty(B_2)}$ (for Proposition \ref{p.localLip-initial-data}).

\emph{Step 1.} We introduce the change of variables
\[u = \phi(v)\]
for some increasing and smooth function $\phi : [0,\infty) \to [0,\infty)$ with $\phi(0) = 0$. Call $\ell(v) := \phi''(v)/\phi'(v)$. Since $\nabla u = \phi'(v)\nabla v$ and $\Delta u = \phi'(v)\Delta v + \phi''(v)|\nabla v|^2$, after the change of variables the equation becomes
\[\partial_t v - \Delta v - \ell(v) |\nabla v|^2 =- k(x,v) \ \hbox{ with } \  k(x,v) := \frac{Q(x)^2 \beta_\varepsilon(\phi(v))}{\phi'(v)} \geq 0 .\]
Differentiating with respect to $x_i$, multiplying by $2\partial_{x_i}v$ and summing over $i$, we find that the quantity $w := |\nabla v|^2$ satisfies
\begin{equation}\label{e.w-eq}
\partial_t w - \Delta w - 2\ell(v)\nabla v\cdot\nabla w = 2\ell'(v) w^2 - 2\partial_v k w - 2\nabla_xk\cdot\nabla v - 2|D^2v|^2 .
\end{equation}
The term $2\ell'(v)w^2$ has been created by the change of variables, and we will choose $\phi$ so that $\ell'(v)$ is negative everywhere and very negative across the transition layer. In particular we will have $2\ell'(v) w^2 = -2|\ell'(v)|w^2$. 

\emph{Step 2.} Put $v_{\max} := \varepsilon + 4M$ and $a := \frac{1}{8v_{\max}^2}$. The following properties of $\phi$ will be used; the construction is postponed to Step 4.
\begin{enumerate}[label = (\alph*)]
    \item\label{phi.a} $\tfrac12 \leq \phi' \leq e$ on $[0,v_{\max}]$, and $\phi(v_{\max}) \geq 2M$.
    \item\label{phi.b} $\phi(\varepsilon) \geq \varepsilon$ so that $\{v < \varepsilon\} = \{\phi^{-1}(u)<\varepsilon\} = \{u < \phi(\varepsilon)\} \supset \{u < \varepsilon\}$.
    \item\label{phi.c} On $[0,\varepsilon]$: $\ell' \leq -\varepsilon^{-2}$, $0 \leq \ell \leq 2/\varepsilon$, and $\phi' \geq 1$.
    \item\label{phi.d} On $[\varepsilon,\infty)$: $\ell' \leq -a$.
    \item\label{phi.e} $\ell^2 \leq 2|\ell'|$ on $[0,v_{\max}]$.
\end{enumerate}
By \ref{phi.a}, $\phi$ maps $[0,v_{\max}]$ onto an interval containing $[0,2M]$, so $v = \phi^{-1}(u)$ is well defined, smooth in $\Gamma$, continuous on $\overline\Gamma$, and takes values in $[0,v_{\max}]$. 


Let us record what these properties give for the coefficients in (\ref{e.w-eq}). In $\{v < \varepsilon\}$ we have
\[k_v = Q^2\Big(\beta_\varepsilon'(u) - \frac{\beta_\varepsilon(u) \ell(v)}{\phi'(v)}\Big), \  \nabla_x k = \frac{\beta_\varepsilon(u) \nabla(Q^2)}{\phi'(v)},\]
and since $|\beta_\varepsilon| \leq \|\beta\|_\infty\varepsilon^{-1}$, $|\beta_\varepsilon'| \leq \|\beta'\|_\infty\varepsilon^{-2}$, $0 \leq \ell \leq 2/\varepsilon$ and $\phi' \geq 1$ there,
\[|k_v| \leq C_1 \varepsilon^{-2}, \  |\nabla_xk| \leq N\|\beta\|_\infty \varepsilon^{-1}, \  C_1 := \|\beta'\|_\infty + 2\|\beta\|_\infty .\]
On $\{v\geq \varepsilon\}$ then $\phi(v) \geq \varepsilon$ by \ref{phi.b} so $\beta_\varepsilon(\phi(v)) \equiv 0$ and $k \equiv 0$.

\emph{Step 3.} We localize with a cutoff $\eta$, $0 \leq \eta \leq 1$, with $|\nabla\eta| + |\partial_t\eta| + |D^2\eta| \leq C_d$. For Proposition \ref{p.localLip} we take $\eta(x,t) = \eta_1(x)\eta_2(t)$ with $\eta_1 \in C^\infty_c(B_2)$, $\eta_1 = 1$ on $B_1$, $\eta_2 = 1$ on $[-1,0]$ and $\eta_2 = 0$ on $(-\infty,-3]$. For Proposition \ref{p.localLip-initial-data} we just cut-off in space $\eta(x,t) = \eta_1(x)$. We consider the quantity
\[z := \eta^2 w .\]
Note that $z$ vanishes where $\eta = 0$. For Proposition \ref{p.localLip} this includes a neighborhood of $\partial_P\Gamma$ and so $z$ is continuous on $\overline \Gamma$. For Proposition \ref{p.localLip-initial-data}, $\eta =0$ on a neighborhood of the spatial boundary $\partial B_2 \times [-\tau_0,0]$, and $\nabla v = \nabla u/\phi'(v)$ extends continuously to $\overline\Gamma$, so still $z$ is continuous on $\overline \Gamma$.

  If $z \equiv 0$ there is nothing to prove. Otherwise $z$ attains a positive maximum at a point $(\hat x,\hat t)$ where $\eta > 0$ and $w > 0$. We will show that
\begin{equation}\label{e.zmax}
z(\hat x,\hat t) \leq \max\big(1, C + 2N\|\beta\|_\infty,\ C(1 + 4M)^2,4L^2\big) .
\end{equation}
If $\hat t = -\tau_0$, which can only happen for Proposition \ref{p.localLip-initial-data}, then by \ref{phi.a} we have $z \leq w = |\nabla u|^2/\phi'(v)^2 \leq 4L^2$ at $(\hat{x},\hat{t})$. Otherwise $(\hat x, \hat t)$ is an interior or final time maximum and the derivative tests hold
\[\partial_t z \geq 0, \nabla z = 0, \hbox{ and } \Delta z \leq 0 .\]
Let us compute $\partial_t z - \Delta z - 2\ell\nabla v\cdot\nabla z$, which is non-negative at $(\hat x,\hat t)$ by the derivative tests. We have
\begin{align*}
\partial_t z - \Delta z - 2\ell\nabla v\cdot\nabla z &= \eta^2\big(\partial_t w - \Delta w - 2\ell\nabla v\cdot\nabla w\big) \\ & \  + w\big(\partial_t\eta^2 - \Delta\eta^2 - 2\ell\nabla v\cdot\nabla\eta^2\big) - 2\nabla\eta^2\cdot\nabla w .
\end{align*}
The first parenthesis is given by (\ref{e.w-eq}). In the second parenthesis, $|\partial_t\eta^2 - \Delta\eta^2| \leq C$, while by Young's inequality and \ref{phi.e},
\[4|\ell| \eta|\nabla\eta| w^{3/2} \leq |\ell'| \eta^2w^2 + \frac{4\ell^2}{|\ell'|}|\nabla\eta|^2w \leq |\ell'| \eta^2w^2 + C w .\]
Finally $|\nabla w| \leq 2|D^2v| w^{1/2}$, so that
\[-2\nabla\eta^2\cdot\nabla w \leq 8\eta|\nabla\eta| |D^2v| w^{1/2} \leq \eta^2|D^2v|^2 + C w.\]
The positive Hessian term is absorbed by the term $-2\eta^2|D^2v|^2$ coming from (\ref{e.w-eq}). Collecting terms, and using the bounds on $k_v$ and $\nabla_xk$ from Step 2, we arrive at
\[0 \leq -|\ell'(v)| \eta^2w^2 + C w + \eta^2\big(2C_1\varepsilon^{-2} w + 2N\|\beta\|_\infty\varepsilon^{-1} w^{1/2}\big) {\bf 1}_{\{v < \varepsilon\}} \  \hbox{at } (\hat x,\hat t) .\]
Dividing by $w > 0$ this reads
\begin{equation}\label{e.zmax-ineq}
|\ell'(v)| z \leq C + \eta^2\big(2C_1\varepsilon^{-2} + 2N\|\beta\|_\infty \varepsilon^{-1}w^{-1/2}\big) {\bf 1}_{\{v < \varepsilon\}} \  \hbox{at } (\hat x,\hat t) .
\end{equation}
We now analyze (\ref{e.zmax-ineq}) separately in the two regions.

  \emph{In $v \geq \varepsilon$.} Here the indicator vanishes and $|\ell'| \geq a$ by \ref{phi.d}, so
\[z \leq \frac{C}{a} = 8C v_{\max}^2 \leq C(1 + 4M)^2 .\]

\emph{In $v < \varepsilon$.} Here $|\ell'| \geq \varepsilon^{-2}$ by \ref{phi.c}, and multiplying (\ref{e.zmax-ineq}) by $\varepsilon^2 \leq 1$ we get
\[z \leq C+C_1 + 2N\|\beta\|_\infty \varepsilon w^{-1/2} .\]
If $w < 1$ then $z \leq \eta^2 w < 1$, and if $w \geq 1$ then $z \leq C+C_1 + 2N\|\beta\|_\infty$. 

This proves (\ref{e.zmax}). Since $w = z$ where $\eta = 1$, which contains $B_1 \times (-1,0]$ for Proposition \ref{p.localLip} and $B_1 \times [-\tau_0,0]$ for Proposition \ref{p.localLip-initial-data}, and since $|\nabla u|^2 = \phi'(v)^2 w \leq e^2 w$ by \ref{phi.a}, the lemma follows from (\ref{e.zmax}) and $M \geq 1$.

\emph{Step 4. Construction of $\phi$.} It is convenient to prescribe $\ell = \phi''/\phi'$ and then recover $\phi$ from $\phi'(v) = \exp\big(\int_0^v \ell\big)$, $\phi(v) = \int_0^v\phi'$. Let $\rho := \varepsilon^2/(64 v_{\max})$, fix a nonincreasing $\psi \in C^\infty(\mathbb{R})$ with $\psi = 1$ on $(-\infty,0]$ and $\psi = 0$ on $[1,\infty)$, and set
\[\ell(v) := \int_v^\varepsilon \Big(\varepsilon^{-2}\psi\Big(\frac{s-\varepsilon}{\rho}\Big) + a\Big) ds, \  \hbox{so that} \  \ell'(v) = -\varepsilon^{-2}\psi\Big(\frac{v-\varepsilon}{\rho}\Big) - a .\]
Thus $\ell' = -\varepsilon^{-2} - a$ on $[0,\varepsilon]$, $\ell' = -a$ on $[\varepsilon + \rho, \infty)$, and $\ell'$ is between these values in the short interval $[\varepsilon, \varepsilon+\rho]$. In particular \ref{phi.d} holds. On $[0,\varepsilon]$ we have $\ell(v) = (\varepsilon^{-2} + a)(\varepsilon - v)$, so $0 \leq \ell \leq (\varepsilon^{-2}+a)\varepsilon \leq 2/\varepsilon$ because $a = \frac{1}{8v_{\max}^2}\le \frac{1}{8\varepsilon^2}$, as $v_{\max} \ge \varepsilon$. Consequently $\phi'$ increases on $[0,\varepsilon]$ from $\phi'(0) = 1$ to
\[\phi'(\varepsilon) = \exp\big(\tfrac12(1 + a\varepsilon^2)\big) \in [e^{1/2}, e],\]
which gives \ref{phi.c}, \ref{phi.b}, and the bounds of \ref{phi.a} on $[0,\varepsilon]$.

For $v \geq \varepsilon$, $\ell$ is negative, and since $0 \leq \psi \leq 1$ vanishes on $[1,\infty)$,
\begin{equation}\label{e.ell-bds-above-ep}
a(v-\varepsilon) \leq -\ell(v) \leq \frac{\rho}{\varepsilon^2} + a(v - \varepsilon) .
\end{equation}
Hence, for $\varepsilon \leq v \leq v_{\max}$, using $(\rho\varepsilon^{-2})^2 = a/512$ and $a v_{\max}^2 = \tfrac18$,
\[\int_\varepsilon^v|\ell| \leq \frac{\rho}{\varepsilon^2} v_{\max} + \frac{a}{2}v_{\max}^2 \leq \frac1{16} + \frac1{16}, \ \hbox{so that} \ \phi'(v) = \phi'(\varepsilon) e^{-\int_\varepsilon^v|\ell|} \geq \frac {\phi'(\varepsilon)}{2} \geq \frac12,\]
while $\phi'(v) \leq \phi'(\varepsilon) \leq e$ by monotonicity. Then $\phi(v_{\max}) \geq \phi(\varepsilon) + \frac{\phi'(\varepsilon)}{2}\cdot 4M \geq 2M$, which completes \ref{phi.a}. Finally, for \ref{phi.e}: on $[0,\varepsilon]$, $\ell^2/|\ell'| = (\varepsilon^{-2} + a)(\varepsilon-v)^2 \leq 1 + a\varepsilon^2 \leq 2$, and on $[\varepsilon,v_{\max}]$, using $|\ell'| \geq a$ and \eqref{e.ell-bds-above-ep},
\[\frac{\ell^2}{|\ell'|} \leq \frac{2\rho^2\varepsilon^{-4}}{a} + 2a(v-\varepsilon)^2 \leq \frac1{256} + 2a v_{\max}^2 \leq \frac12 .\]
This completes the construction and the proof in the case $\varepsilon \leq 1$.

\emph{Step 5.}  Finally we mention how to handle the case $\varepsilon \geq 1$. In this case no change of variables is needed. The nonlinearity satisfies $\|Q^2\beta_\varepsilon\|_{C^1} \leq \|\beta\|_{C^1}$, and the classical Bernstein argument applies. Take $w := |\nabla u|^2$ then $(\partial_t - \Delta)w \leq 2\|\beta'\|_\infty w + 2N\|\beta\|_\infty w^{1/2}$. Note also that $(\partial_t - \Delta)u^2 = -2Q^2\beta_\varepsilon(u)u - 2w \leq -2w$. So that, with $\eta$ as in Step 3 and $\lambda$ large depending on $d$, $N$ and $\|\beta\|_{C^1}$, the function $z= \eta^2w + \lambda u^2 - \lambda t$ is a subsolution of the heat equation in $\Gamma$. Applying the maximum principle to $z$ gives the result.
<!-- end proof-28 -->
<!-- head-18: body_md -->

<!-- end head-19 -->
<!-- head-20: body_md -->

<!-- head-21: body_md -->
