<!-- proposition-10: body_md -->
Let $g_\varepsilon$ be non-negative, $L$-Lipschitz on $\overline{U}$, and bounded above by $M$. Assume that $\mathfrak{u}_\varepsilon \in C(\overline{U_\infty})$ is a classical solution of \eqref{e.bernoulli-parabolic-semilinear}. There is a modulus of continuity $\varpi$, independent of $\varepsilon \in (0,1]$ and of $t$, such that for all $(x,t)$ and $(y,s)$ in $\overline{U_\infty}$
 \[ |\mathfrak{u}_\varepsilon(x,t) - \mathfrak{u}_\varepsilon(y,s)| \leq \varpi(|x-y|+|t-s|).\]
<!-- end proposition-10 -->
<!-- lemma-20: body_md -->
\label{l.attainment-lateral}
Under the same hypotheses as Proposition \ref{p.attainment} there is a modulus of continuity $\varpi$, independent of $\varepsilon \in (0,1]$ and of $t$, so that for all $x,y \in \overline{U}$ and any $t \geq 0$
\[ |\mathfrak{u}_\varepsilon(x,t) - \mathfrak{u}_\varepsilon(y,t)| \leq \varpi(|x-y|).\]
<!-- end lemma-20 -->
<!-- proof-29: body_md -->
We aim to show that for every $x_0 \in \partial U$, $x \in \overline U$, and $t > 0$,
\[ |\mathfrak{u}_\varepsilon(x,t) - g_\varepsilon(x_0)| \leq \varpi(|x - x_0|).\]
Assuming we have this it is easy to derive the result by arguing as in Lemma \ref{l.lipschitz-initial} and combining the interior Lipschitz estimate with the boundary modulus. 



Let $h_\varepsilon$ be the harmonic function in $U$ with $h_\varepsilon = g_\varepsilon$ on $\partial U$. Then $h_\varepsilon$ is a stationary supersolution of \eqref{e.bernoulli-parabolic-semilinear} with $h_\varepsilon \geq \mathfrak{u}_\varepsilon$ on $\partial _PU$ so $h_\varepsilon \geq \mathfrak{u}_\varepsilon$ in $U \times (0,\infty)$. Since $U$ is a $C^2$ regular domain there is a modulus of continuity $\varpi_0$ depending only on $L$ and $M$ so that $|h_\varepsilon(x) - g_\varepsilon(x_0)| \leq \varpi_0(|x-x_0|)$ for $x_0 \in \partial U$ and $x \in U$. This gives the upper bound inequality 
\[\mathfrak{u}_\varepsilon(x,t) \leq h_\varepsilon(x) \leq g_\varepsilon(x_0) + \varpi_0(|x-x_0|). \]

For the lower bound we need to redo the standard barrier argument for harmonic functions, we will create a barrier which is a smooth strict subsolution of \eqref{e.bernoulli-parabolic} and then compose with $\Phi_{\varepsilon,\theta}$ to create a subsolution of \eqref{e.bernoulli-parabolic-semilinear}. Let $x_0 \in \partial U$ and assume that $g(x_0)>0$, otherwise the lower bound is trivial. Let $\eta$ be a standard barrier for the Dirichlet problem at $x_0$. Specifically, say $x_0$ has an exterior ball of radius $\rho>0$ centered at $y_0$ then define $\eta(x) = 1-\rho^{d-1}|x - y_0|^{-(d-1)}$. Define $V := U \cap B_{3\rho}(x_0)$ and $\rho \leq |x - y_0| \leq 4\rho$ on $\overline V$. Then $\eta$ satisfies
\begin{enumerate}[label = (\roman*)]
\item\label{part.eta-superharmonic} $\Delta \eta  <0 $ in $\mathbb{R}^d \setminus \{y_0\}$,
\item\label{part.eta-gradient} $c \leq \rho|\nabla \eta| \leq C$ on $\overline V$ and so $\eta(x)\leq C \rho^{-1}|x - x_0|$ on $\overline V$,
\item\label{part.quadratic-behavior} $\eta(x) \geq \tfrac12\big(1 - \tfrac{\rho^2}{|x-y_0|^2}\big) = \tfrac{|x-y_0|^2 - \rho^2}{2|x-y_0|^2} \geq \tfrac{|x-x_0|^2}{64 \rho^2}$ for $x \in \overline V$, using (\ref{e.exterior-ball}) and the elementary inequality $1 - r^{q} \geq \tfrac12(1-r)$ for $r \in [0,1]$, $q \geq \tfrac12$,
\item $\eta \geq 2^{-(d-1)} \geq \tfrac12$ on $U \cap \partial B_{3\rho}(x_0)$, since $|x - y_0| \geq |x-x_0| - \rho = 2\rho$ there.
\end{enumerate}
Let $0<\sigma < 1$ and define
\[ w(x) := g_\varepsilon(x_0) - \sigma -A_\sigma \eta(x).\]
Our eventual goal is to show that $\mathfrak{u}_\varepsilon(x,t) \geq w(x)$ via a comparison argument. If $\sigma \geq g_\varepsilon(x_0)$ this is trivial, so we can assume that $\sigma < g_\varepsilon(x_0)$. 

We will first show that $w$ is a smooth strict subsolution of \eqref{e.bernoulli-basic} in $\overline{U}$. Then we will compose with $w_\varepsilon = \Phi_{\varepsilon,\theta}(w)$ to get a strict subsolution of \eqref{e.bernoulli-parabolic-semilinear}. Then we will argue that $w_\varepsilon \leq g_\varepsilon$ on $\partial_P U_\infty$ in order to do a comparison argument and conclude.

From \ref{part.eta-superharmonic} $w$ is a smooth subharmonic function on $\overline{U}$. On $\overline{U}  \setminus B_{2\rho}(x_0)$
\begin{equation}\label{e.b2rho-outside}
w(x) \leq g_\varepsilon(x_0) - \sigma - cA_\sigma \leq -c_{1/2} \leq 0 \ \hbox{ if } \ A_\sigma \geq C(1+M).
\end{equation}
Here $c_{1/2}$ is the constant from Lemma \ref{l.profile-sub}. In particular $w(x) \leq 0 \leq g_\varepsilon(x)$ on $\overline{U}  \setminus B_{2\rho}(x_0)$. Next we claim that $w \leq g_\varepsilon$ on $\overline{U}\cap B_{2\rho}(x_0)$.  Indeed by the Lipschitz bound ${g}_\varepsilon(x) \geq {g}_\varepsilon(x_0) - L|x-x_0|$, so it suffices that $\sigma + A_\sigma\eta(x) \geq L|x-x_0|$.  By \ref{part.quadratic-behavior}
\[\sigma + A_\sigma\eta(x) \geq \sigma + cA_\sigma \rho^{-2}|x-x_0|^2 \geq c\rho^{-1}\sqrt{\sigma A_\sigma} |x-x_0| \geq L|x-x_0|,\]
if we choose $A_\sigma \geq C L^2\rho^2/\sigma$.  Finally from \ref{part.eta-gradient} on $B_{3\rho}(x_0) \cap \overline{U}$
\[|\nabla w| = A_\sigma|\nabla \eta| \geq cA_\sigma\rho^{-1} \geq 2Q_{\max}\] 
 as long as we choose $A_\sigma \geq C\rho Q_{\max}$.

 Thus $w$ is a smooth strict subsolution of \eqref{e.bernoulli-basic} in $\overline{U}$ with $w \leq g_\varepsilon$ on $\overline{U}$.  By Lemma \ref{l.well-prepared} there is $\theta \in (0,1)$, as per Lemma \ref{l.well-prepared} $\theta = 1/2$ works, so that $w_\varepsilon(x) := (\Phi_{\varepsilon,\theta}(w(x)))_+$ is a stationary viscosity subsolution of \eqref{e.bernoulli-parabolic-semilinear}. By Lemma \ref{l.profile-sub}\ref{part.profile-sub-a} where $w(x) \geq \varepsilon$ we get
 \[ w_\varepsilon(x) = (\Phi_{\varepsilon,\theta}(w(x)))_+ = w(x) \leq g_\varepsilon(x).\]
 Where $w(x) \leq -c_\theta \varepsilon$ then Lemma \ref{l.profile-sub}\ref{part.profile-sub-c} gives $w_\varepsilon(x) = 0 \leq g_\varepsilon(x)$.  Finally, suppose $-c_\theta\varepsilon \leq w(x) \leq \varepsilon$.
By \eqref{e.b2rho-outside} such a point lies in
$B_{2\rho}(x_0)$, and \ref{part.quadratic-behavior} gives
\[
\frac{A_\sigma}{64\rho^2}|x-x_0|^2
\leq A_\sigma\eta(x)
= g_\varepsilon(x_0)-\sigma-w(x)
\leq g_\varepsilon(x_0)+c_\theta\varepsilon
\leq 2g_\varepsilon(x_0).
\]
Since $\sigma<g_\varepsilon(x_0)$, increasing the constant in
$A_\sigma\geq CL^2\rho^2/\sigma$ ensures that
$L|x-x_0|\leq g_\varepsilon(x_0)/2$. Consequently, by the Lipschitz
continuity of $g_\varepsilon$ and
Lemma \ref{l.profile-sub}\ref{part.profile-sub-c},
\[
w_\varepsilon(x)\leq w(x)_+ + \varepsilon
\leq 2\varepsilon
\leq \frac{g_\varepsilon(x_0)}{2}
\leq g_\varepsilon(x_0)-L|x-x_0|
\leq g_\varepsilon(x).
\]



 Thus we have shown that $w_\varepsilon \leq g_\varepsilon$ everywhere in $\overline{U}$, by comparison principle for \eqref{e.bernoulli-parabolic-semilinear} we conclude that $ \mathfrak{u}_\varepsilon(x,t) \geq w_\varepsilon(x,t) \geq w(x,t)$ on $U_\infty$.

 Then applying \ref{part.eta-gradient} we conclude, absorbing the extra $\rho^{-1}$ factor into the universal constant $C$,
 \[ \mathfrak{u}_\varepsilon(x,t) \geq g_\varepsilon(x_0) - \sigma - CA_\sigma |x-x_0| .\]
Taking $\varpi(r) := \inf_{\sigma \in (0,1)}\big(\sigma + CA_\sigma  r\big)$, which is a modulus of continuity, finishes the proof.
<!-- end proof-29 -->
<!-- lemma-21: body_md -->
\label{l.initial-L2}
Let $g_\varepsilon$ be Lipschitz continuous and bounded on $\overline{U}$. For every $\varepsilon \in (0,\varepsilon_0]$ and $t ,s\geq 0$,
\[\|\mathfrak{u}_\varepsilon(\cdot,t) - \mathfrak{u}_\varepsilon(\cdot,s)\|_{L^2(U)} \leq \Big(\tfrac{1}{2}E_0  |t-s|\Big)^{1/2}.\]
<!-- end lemma-21 -->
<!-- proof-30: body_md -->
Take $t>s$. By \eqref{eqn:dissipation} and Lemma \ref{l.well-prepared}(iv), $$\int_0^\infty\int_U (\partial_t \mathfrak{u}_\varepsilon)^2  dx  dt \leq \tfrac12 J(g_\varepsilon,\chi^0_\varepsilon;U) \leq \tfrac12 E_0.$$ Since $\mathfrak{u}_\varepsilon \in C([0,\infty);L^2(U))$ with $\partial_t \mathfrak{u}_\varepsilon \in L^2(U\times(0,t))$, the fundamental theorem of calculus in $L^2$ and the Cauchy--Schwarz inequality give
\begin{multline}
\int_U |\mathfrak{u}_\varepsilon(x,t) - \mathfrak{u}_\varepsilon(\cdot,s)|^2   dx = \int_U \Big|\int_s^t \partial_\tau \mathfrak{u}_\varepsilon(x,\tau)  d\tau\Big|^2 dx \\
\leq (t-s) \int_s^t \int_U (\partial_s \mathfrak{u}_\varepsilon)^2   dx  d\tau \leq \tfrac12 E_0  (t-s). 
\end{multline}
This includes the case $s=0$ where $\mathfrak{u}_\varepsilon(\cdot,s)=g_\varepsilon(\cdot)$.
<!-- end proof-30 -->
<!-- proof-31: body_md -->
Combining $L^2$ continuity in time Lemma \ref{l.initial-L2} with the uniform modulus of continuity in space from Lemma \ref{l.attainment-lateral} gives the continuity in $L^\infty$ norm with a uniform modulus independent of $t$.  The proof is elementary, if $\|\mathfrak{u}_\varepsilon(\cdot,t) - \mathfrak{u}_\varepsilon(\cdot,s)\|_{L^\infty(U)} =: \delta>0$ then $|\mathfrak{u}_\varepsilon(\cdot,t) - \mathfrak{u}_\varepsilon(\cdot,s)| \geq \frac{\delta}{2}$ in a $\varpi^{-1}(\delta/2)$ radius ball centered somewhere in $\overline{U}$.  Plugging into Lemma \ref{l.initial-L2} gives the bound $C|t-s|^{1/2} \geq c\varpi^{-1}(\delta/2)^{d/2}\delta$ and inverting this relation gives the modulus of continuity, up to updating $\varpi$ again.
<!-- end proof-31 -->
<!-- lemma-22: body_md -->
\label{l.positivity-trace}
Let $g_\varepsilon$ be Lipschitz continuous and bounded on $\overline{U}$ and let $\mathfrak{u}_\varepsilon$ be the solution of \eqref{e.bernoulli-parabolic-semilinear}. Suppose that $x_0 \in \overline{U}$ and $B_{3r}(x_0) \cap \overline{U} \subset \{g_\varepsilon \leq (1-\mu)\varepsilon\}$ for some $ \mu \in (0,1)$.  Then there exists $\tau>0$ and $\varepsilon_0>0$ depending only on $r$, $\mu$, and universal parameters so that $\overline{B_{r}(x_0)} \subset \{\mathfrak{u}_\varepsilon(x,t) \leq \varepsilon\}$ for all $ 0 \leq t \leq \tau$ and $0 < \varepsilon \leq \varepsilon_0$.
<!-- end lemma-22 -->
<!-- corollary-5: body_md -->
\label{c.positivity-no-jump}
Let $g$ be a smooth strict subsolution of \eqref{e.bernoulli-basic}, $g_\varepsilon = (\Phi_{\varepsilon,\theta}(g))_+$ as in Lemma \ref{l.well-prepared}, and $\mathfrak{u}_\varepsilon$ be the corresponding solution of \eqref{e.bernoulli-parabolic-semilinear}. Suppose that $x_0 \in \overline{U}$ and $B_{4r}(x_0) \cap \overline{U} \subset \{g \leq 0\}$.  Then there exists $\tau>0$ depending only on $r$ and universal parameters so that 
\[B_r(x_0) \times [0,\tau] \subset \overline{U} \setminus ({\limsup_{\varepsilon \to 0}}^*\{\mathfrak{u}_\varepsilon>\varepsilon\}).\]
<!-- end corollary-5 -->
<!-- proof-32: body_md -->
By Lemma \ref{l.well-prepared}\ref{part.gep-5} $\{g_\varepsilon>0\} \subset \{g > -c \varepsilon\}$ and since $g$ is a subsolution with $|\nabla g| \geq Q_{\min}$ on $\partial \{g>0\}$ we conclude that $\{g>-c\varepsilon\} \subset \{g>0\}+B_{C\varepsilon}$. In particular for $\varepsilon>0$ sufficiently small $B_{3r}(x_0) \subset \{g_\varepsilon = 0\}$. Then Proposition \ref{p.positivity-trace} applies and there exists $\tau>0$ depending on $r>0$ and universal parameters so that $\overline{B_r(x_0)} \times [0,\tau] \subset \overline{U} \setminus \{\mathfrak{u}_\varepsilon > \varepsilon\}$ and the containment with the ${\limsup}^*$ follows.
<!-- end proof-32 -->
<!-- proof-33: body_md -->
By the definition of $\kappa_{\hat \theta}$ in \eqref{e.kappa-def}, and the comment below that displayed equation, we can choose $\hat \theta$ sufficiently large so that $\kappa_{\hat \theta} = 1-\frac{1}{2}\mu$.  

Let $\eta$ be a radial strictly superharmonic function in $B_3 \setminus B_{3/2}$ which is zero on $\partial B_{2}$ and $1$ on $\partial B_3$. Extend $\eta$ in a smooth monotone radial way to be equal to $-1$ on $B_{1}$. Call $c_0(d)$ to be supremum of $|\nabla \eta|$ on $B_{2} \setminus B_{3/2}$. Let $\gamma>0$ sufficiently small so that $\gamma c_0 \leq \frac{1}{2}Q_{\min}$. Then call $\hat\eta(x) = \gamma r\eta(\frac{x-x_0}{r})$, this is a smooth strict supersolution of \eqref{e.bernoulli-basic} in $B_3$ with parameters $\delta_0 = \frac{1}{2}$ and $a_0 = \frac{1}{2}$.  Choosing $\hat{\theta}$ larger if necessary we can also guarantee $\hat\theta \geq 2 = \frac{1}{1-\delta_0}$, as needed for applying Lemma \ref{l.well-prepared}.

Then define $\hat \eta_\varepsilon = \Psi_{\varepsilon,\hat\theta}(\hat \eta)$. By Lemma \ref{l.well-prepared} we conclude that $\hat \eta_\varepsilon$ is a supersolution of \eqref{e.bernoulli-parabolic-semilinear} in $B_{2r}(x_0)$. By choice of $\hat\theta$ and Lemma \ref{l.profile-super} we have $\hat \eta_\varepsilon \geq \kappa_{\hat \theta} = 1-\frac{1}{2}\mu \geq g_\varepsilon$ on $B_{2r}(x_0)$.  By Proposition \ref{p.attainment} $\mathfrak{u}_\varepsilon(x,t) \leq \delta r \leq \hat \eta_\varepsilon(x)$ on $\partial B_{2r}(x_0)$ for $t \leq \tau$ and $\tau$ sufficiently small so that $\varpi(\tau) \leq r \delta$.  Since $\delta>0$ depends only on $\mu$, $\tau$ depends only on $r$ and $\mu$.  Thus comparison principle for \eqref{e.bernoulli-parabolic-semilinear} on $B_{2r}(x_0) \times (0,\tau]$ yields $\mathfrak{u}_\varepsilon(x,t) \leq \hat \eta_\varepsilon(x)$ in $B_{2r}(x_0) \times (0,\tau]$. Since $\hat \eta \leq - \delta r$ in $B_{r/2}$ and using Lemma \ref{l.profile-super} we get $\hat \eta_\varepsilon  \leq \kappa \varepsilon+Ce^{-c\delta r/\varepsilon} \leq \varepsilon$ for $\varepsilon>0$ sufficiently small depending on $\delta$ and $r$.
<!-- end proof-33 -->
<!-- theorem-6: body_md -->
\label{t.largest-sub-non-degen}
    If $d=2$ and $u$ is a largest subsolution in $B_1(0)$ and $0 \in \partial \{u>0\}$ then for all $0 < r \leq 1$
    \[ \sup_{\partial B_r(0)} u \geq c r.\]
<!-- end theorem-6 -->
<!-- lemma-23: body_md -->
\label{l.outer-reg-non-degen}
    If $u$ is a subsolution of \eqref{e.bernoulli-basic} in $B_1(0)$ and $\{u>0\}$ has an exterior touching ball of radius $1$ at $0 \in \partial \{u>0\}$ then
    \[ \max_{\partial B_1(0)} u \geq c.\]
<!-- end lemma-23 -->
<!-- lemma-24: body_md -->
\label{l.nondegen-equivalences}
    Suppose that $u$ a non-negative Lipschitz continuous function on $B_1(0)$ which is harmonic in $\{u>0\}$ with $0  \in \partial \{u>0\}$ and satisfying for some $c_i>0$ one of the following conditions:
    \begin{enumerate}[label = (\roman*)]
        \item\label{part.avg} There exists $c_1>0$ so that 
        \[\mathchoice
{{\setbox0=\hbox{$\displaystyle{\textstyle-}{\int}$ }
\vcenter{\hbox{$\textstyle-$ }}\kern-.6\wd0}} 
{{\setbox0=\hbox{$\textstyle{\scriptstyle-}{\int}$ }
\vcenter{\hbox{$\scriptstyle-$ }}\kern-.6\wd0}} 
{{\setbox0=\hbox{$\scriptstyle{\scriptscriptstyle-}{\int}$ }
\vcenter{\hbox{$\scriptscriptstyle-$ }}\kern-.6\wd0}} 
{{\setbox0=\hbox{$\scriptscriptstyle{\scriptscriptstyle-}{\int}$ }
\vcenter{\hbox{$\scriptscriptstyle-$ }}\kern-.6\wd0}} 
\!\int_{\partial B_r(0)} u(x)~dS(x) \geq c_1 r \ \hbox{ for } \ 0 < r < 1\]
        \item\label{part.sup} There exists $c_2>0$ so that 
        \[ \sup_{\partial B_r(0)} u \geq c_2 r \ \hbox{ for } \ 0 < r < 1.\]
        \item\label{part.laplace} There exists $c_3,\kappa>0$ so that 
        \[\int_{B_r(0)} \Delta u ~dx \geq c_3 r^{d-1} \ \hbox{ for } \ 0 < r < 1.\]
    \end{enumerate}
    Then the other two conditions $ j \in \{\ref{part.avg},\ref{part.sup},\ref{part.laplace}\}$ for $j \neq i$ also hold with constants $c_j$ depending only on $c_i$, $d$ and $L$.
<!-- end lemma-24 -->
<!-- proof-34: body_md -->
Note that \ref{part.avg} implies \ref{part.sup} immediately. The other direction \ref{part.sup} implies \ref{part.avg} follows from the Lipschitz estimate. So it suffices to show \ref{part.avg} is equivalent to \ref{part.laplace}.

Note that
\[ \frac{d}{dr}\mathchoice
{{\setbox0=\hbox{$\displaystyle{\textstyle-}{\int}$ }
\vcenter{\hbox{$\textstyle-$ }}\kern-.6\wd0}} 
{{\setbox0=\hbox{$\textstyle{\scriptstyle-}{\int}$ }
\vcenter{\hbox{$\scriptstyle-$ }}\kern-.6\wd0}} 
{{\setbox0=\hbox{$\scriptstyle{\scriptscriptstyle-}{\int}$ }
\vcenter{\hbox{$\scriptscriptstyle-$ }}\kern-.6\wd0}} 
{{\setbox0=\hbox{$\scriptscriptstyle{\scriptscriptstyle-}{\int}$ }
\vcenter{\hbox{$\scriptscriptstyle-$ }}\kern-.6\wd0}} 
\!\int_{\partial B_r(0)} u(x)~dS(x) = \frac{1}{|\partial B_1| r^{d-1}} \int_{B_r(0)} \Delta u ~dx\]
so
\[0 = u(0) = \mathchoice
{{\setbox0=\hbox{$\displaystyle{\textstyle-}{\int}$ }
\vcenter{\hbox{$\textstyle-$ }}\kern-.6\wd0}} 
{{\setbox0=\hbox{$\textstyle{\scriptstyle-}{\int}$ }
\vcenter{\hbox{$\scriptstyle-$ }}\kern-.6\wd0}} 
{{\setbox0=\hbox{$\scriptstyle{\scriptscriptstyle-}{\int}$ }
\vcenter{\hbox{$\scriptscriptstyle-$ }}\kern-.6\wd0}} 
{{\setbox0=\hbox{$\scriptscriptstyle{\scriptscriptstyle-}{\int}$ }
\vcenter{\hbox{$\scriptscriptstyle-$ }}\kern-.6\wd0}} 
\!\int_{\partial B_r(0)} u(x)~dS(x) -\frac{1}{|\partial B_1|}\int_0^r\frac{1}{s^{d-1}} \int_{B_s(0)} \Delta u ~dx~ds.\]
From this it is direct to show that \ref{part.laplace} implies \ref{part.avg}. 

Finally to show that \ref{part.avg} implies \ref{part.laplace} use that
\begin{align*}
    \frac{1}{|\partial B_1|}\int_{\kappa r}^r\frac{1}{s^{d-1}} \int_{B_s(0)} \Delta u ~dx~ds &= \mathchoice
{{\setbox0=\hbox{$\displaystyle{\textstyle-}{\int}$ }
\vcenter{\hbox{$\textstyle-$ }}\kern-.6\wd0}} 
{{\setbox0=\hbox{$\textstyle{\scriptstyle-}{\int}$ }
\vcenter{\hbox{$\scriptstyle-$ }}\kern-.6\wd0}} 
{{\setbox0=\hbox{$\scriptstyle{\scriptscriptstyle-}{\int}$ }
\vcenter{\hbox{$\scriptscriptstyle-$ }}\kern-.6\wd0}} 
{{\setbox0=\hbox{$\scriptscriptstyle{\scriptscriptstyle-}{\int}$ }
\vcenter{\hbox{$\scriptscriptstyle-$ }}\kern-.6\wd0}} 
\!\int_{\partial B_r(0)} u(x)~dS(x) - \mathchoice
{{\setbox0=\hbox{$\displaystyle{\textstyle-}{\int}$ }
\vcenter{\hbox{$\textstyle-$ }}\kern-.6\wd0}} 
{{\setbox0=\hbox{$\textstyle{\scriptstyle-}{\int}$ }
\vcenter{\hbox{$\scriptstyle-$ }}\kern-.6\wd0}} 
{{\setbox0=\hbox{$\scriptstyle{\scriptscriptstyle-}{\int}$ }
\vcenter{\hbox{$\scriptscriptstyle-$ }}\kern-.6\wd0}} 
{{\setbox0=\hbox{$\scriptscriptstyle{\scriptscriptstyle-}{\int}$ }
\vcenter{\hbox{$\scriptscriptstyle-$ }}\kern-.6\wd0}} 
\!\int_{\partial B_{\kappa r}(0)} u(x)~dS(x) \\
    &\geq (c-L\kappa) r \geq \frac{1}{2}cr
\end{align*}
 choosing $\kappa = \frac{1}{2L}c$.  On the other hand, since $\Delta u$ is a non-negative measure,
 \[\frac{1}{|\partial B_1|}\int_{\kappa r}^r\frac{1}{s^{d-1}} \int_{B_s(0)} \Delta u ~dx~ds \leq \frac{1}{|\partial B_1|\kappa^{d-1}}\frac{1}{r^{d-2}}\int_{B_r(0)} \Delta u ~dx\]
<!-- end proof-34 -->
<!-- lemma-25: body_md -->
If $u$ is a largest subsolution in $B_1$ and $0 \in \partial \{u>0\}$ then for any $0 < r < 1$, $ \partial B_r(0) \setminus \overline{\{u>0\}} \neq \emptyset$.
<!-- end lemma-25 -->
<!-- proof-35: body_md -->
Suppose, towards a contradiction, that $\partial B_r(0) \subset \overline{\{u>0\}}$. Let $v$ be the harmonic lift of $u$ in $B_r(0)$ which is equal to $u$ outside of $B_r(0)$.  Since $u$ is harmonic in $\{u>0\} \cap U$ and non-negative $u$ is subharmonic in $U$. Thus $u \leq v $ in $B$.  Since $0 \in \partial \{u>0\} \subset \{u=0\}$ we must have $v > u$ in $B$ by strong maximum principle. We claim that $v$ is a subsolution of (\ref{e.bernoulli-basic}) in $\{v>u\} \cup U \setminus \overline{\{u>0\}}$. Note that by the hypotheses $\partial B$ does not intersect this set so nothing needs to be checked there.  Thus the largest subsolution property of $u$ implies that $v \leq u$ which is a contradiction.
<!-- end proof-35 -->
<!-- proof-36: body_md -->
By Lemma~\ref{l.nondegen-equivalences} it suffices to show that $\int_{B_r(0)} \Delta u \geq cr$ for all $0 < r < 1$. By hyperbolic scaling invariance of the largest subsolution property it suffices to show $\int_{B_1(0)} \Delta u \geq c$.
    
    For all $0 < r < 1$ there is $x_r \in \partial B_r(0) \setminus E$ and let $\rho_r = d(x,E)$. Then $B_{\rho_r}(x_r)$ touches $\{u>0\}$ from the outside at some point $y_r$ so Lemma \ref{l.outer-reg-non-degen} and Lemma~\ref{l.nondegen-equivalences} imply that 
    \[\int_{B_{2\rho_r}(x_r)}  \Delta u \geq c\rho_r. \]
    Since $\{(r-2\rho_r,r+2\rho_r)\}_{r \in (0,1]}$ form an open cover of $(0,1]$ there is a disjoint subcollection $\{(r_j-\rho_j,r_j+\rho_j)\}_{j=1}^\infty$ such that $(r_j - 10\rho_j,r_j+10\rho_j)$ covers $(0,1]$. Note that the disjointness of the intervals of radii implies disjointness of the balls $B_{2\rho_j}(x_{r_j})$. Thus
    \[ \sum 20\rho_j \geq 1 \ \hbox{ and so } \ \int_{B_1(0)} \Delta u \geq \sum_j \int_{B_{2\rho_j}(x_{r_j})} \Delta u \geq c \sum \rho_j \geq c.\]
    This concludes the proof
<!-- end proof-36 -->
